source.title: Functoriality, Smith theory, and the Brauer homomorphism
readSections: Read in full from the arXiv source (arXiv:1407.2346v1, 9 July 2014, the only version; source archive sha256 28e20b81414249488dc37189de7ffeb316314c5c3ea374fe675a5e28195b2c11, file TV_submit.tex, 5733 lines): §1 Introduction, §2 Notation, §3 Tate cohomology, §4 The Brauer homomorphism, §5 Cyclic group actions on locally symmetric spaces, §6 Representation theory, §7 Satake parameters, §8 The Satake parameters of the Brauer homomorphism, §9–12 Construction of σ-dual homomorphisms 1–4.

All locators refer to the preprint. The preprint numbers theorems, propositions, lemmas and definitions by the subsection counter (\newtheorem{theorem}[subsection]{Theorem}), so statement numbers interleave with subsection numbers and many statements are unnumbered; an unnumbered statement is located by its subsection and its position in it.

The published version could not be read, so no published numbering map was built and no claim is made here about the printed text. The Annals of Mathematics article page serves the text only as a PDF; that PDF (annals-v183-n1-p04-p.pdf) downloads freely but is encrypted with the standard security handler (/Filter /Standard /V 2 /Length 128), so its content streams cannot be decompressed and its text cannot be read. No PDF text-extraction tool is installed in this environment either (pdftotext, mutool, gs, qpdf, pypdf, PyPDF2, fitz, pdfminer and pdfplumber are all absent), but that is not the obstacle: a text extractor written for the purpose does read unencrypted PDFs, and was checked on the arXiv PDF of this very paper, which it reads in full. The encryption of the published PDF is the reason the printed text is not cited here.

Checks run on the source: a duplicate-label audit (no duplicate \label), an undefined-reference audit (none), and a cross-reference type audit comparing the word before each \ref with the environment carrying that label, which found the two occurrences recorded in the source issues below; and a direct computation in the E_8 root system verifying §12.2 (the order and Weyl-group membership of U, the A_3 x A_3 Dynkin diagram of x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_2,y_3, the Coxeter factorisation of U, and the roots of L_G(U) and L_G(U^2)).

Review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): the published version (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 177–228; https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n1-p04-p.pdf, 52 pp., SHA-256 15513cab…) read in full with four checkers and compared with the preprint (the same source archive, SHA-256 28e20b81…), and every item located in both versions. The published version keeps §§1–8 and replaces the preprint's §§9–12 with a §9 of examples.

summary: The paper constructs a mod p transfer of automorphic forms from H = G^σ to G, for σ an F-rational automorphism of prime order p of a semisimple group G over a number field with connected fixed points, and shows in most cases that it is functorial for a homomorphism of L-groups. Mod p automorphic forms are Hecke eigenclasses in the cohomology of congruence subgroups with coefficients in an algebraic closure k of F_p, with no assumption that they lift to characteristic zero. The transfer is a variant of the Brauer homomorphism of modular representation theory: Br restricts a σ-invariant Hecke operator from G/K × G/K to the σ-fixed points, and its normalization nBr is the unique k-linear map agreeing with Br^p on the F_p-form. The First Main Theorem (Theorem 5.8) says that every Hecke eigensystem χ occurring in H^*([H]_U) gives the eigensystem χ ∘ nBr occurring in H^*([G]_K); it is proved by Smith theory, that is Z/p-equivariant fixed-point localisation applied to the locally symmetric space of G, kept Hecke-equivariant through a double complex. Theorem 6.5 describes the ramified places through a notion of linkage defined by Tate cohomology. The Theorem of §8.1 computes nBr on Satake parameters as a dual norm attached to a γ-admissible Borel class, and the Second Main Theorem (Theorem 9.1) constructs a σ-dual homomorphism ^LH → ^LG whenever G is simply connected and H semisimple, outside three excluded factors, by a long case-by-case analysis of prime-order automorphisms. A special case is cyclic base change for torsion classes, which does not follow from classical base change. What the atlas lacks: Smith theory and equivariant localisation in any form; Tate cohomology of a group action on sheaves over l-spaces and on Hecke algebras; the Brauer homomorphism; the characteristic-p normalization of the Satake isomorphism, pseudoroots, and the C-group and c-group; and the structure theory of prime-order automorphisms of reductive groups in characteristic p — Borel-de Siebenthal, the endoscopic subgroups of the dual group, admissible Borels, dual norms and the exceptional isogenies used to build σ-dual homomorphisms. What it already has: Tate cohomology of a finite group with its long exact sequence and 2-periodicity, Witt vectors, and the double-coset Hecke ring with its anti-involution. After the review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16) there are 121 items (4 library, 15 planned, 102 missing) and 53 source issues, and every item carries its published locator or is marked as absent from print. The published version keeps §§1–8 but omits the preprint's σ-dual existence theorem and its proof (§§9–12), announcing it in §1.3. The preprint's proof leaves Theorem 12.1(i)–(iii) unproved. The review found an incorrect explicit formula (4.3.1) for nBr, which is not used later. It found a convergence gap in the proof of Theorem 4.4, repaired by using a bounded complex. It found inverted q_v-normalisations in §§7.2–7.4. Theorems 4.4, 5.8, 6.5 and 8.10 stand.

items.name: Witt vectors of an algebraic closure of F_p
items.statement: For p prime and k an algebraic closure of F_p, W = W(k) is the ring of Witt vectors of k, a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser p and residue field k, and W[1/p] its fraction field; reduction mod p is written x ↦ x-bar.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.1; published version: §2.1 (Notation used throughout), p. 183
items.note: Mathlib has Witt vectors of a commutative ring of characteristic p, with the ring structure, the Teichmueller lift, Frobenius and Verschiebung, and the discrete-valuation-ring statements for a perfect field. Review note: Status library confirmed at 082e2d3: WittVector (RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52), WittVector.frobenius (Frobenius.lean:221), WittVector.teichmuller (Teichmuller.lean:93), WittVector.isDiscreteValuationRing (DiscreteValuationRing.lean:149, for a perfect field such as k). Both versions write Λ for W(k) and Λ[p^-1] for its fraction field; the item's 'W' clashes with the k-vector space W of item 2 (W^(p)) and should be renamed Λ (also in item 23). Statement unchanged between versions.

items.name: Frobenius twist of a k-vector space
items.statement: For W a vector space over a field k of characteristic p, W^(p) is the k-vector space with the same underlying additive group and scalar multiplication λ * w = λ^{1/p} · w; equivalently W^(p) = W ⊗_{(k,Frob)} k, so that wλ ⊗ μ = w ⊗ λ^p μ.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.1; published version: §2.1 (Notation used throughout), p. 184
items.note: Requires k perfect for the 1/p-th power to be defined. Used to state linkage (Definition 6.2), where the Frobenius twist of a representation of H_v appears in the Tate cohomology of a representation of G_v. Review note: Statement identical in both versions and checked on the page image (λ*w = λ^{1/p}·w; W^(p) = W ⊗_(k,Frob) k with wλ⊗μ = w⊗λ^pμ; the two descriptions agree). 'missing' is defensible: Mathlib has the ingredients (Module.compHom along (frobeniusEquiv k p).symm, FieldTheory/Perfect.lean:121, or base change along frobenius) but no named Frobenius twist. Consumer: Definition 6.2 (linkage), published p. 201.

items.name: Nonabelian cohomology of a cyclic group of order p
items.statement: For σ an automorphism of order p of a group M, H^1(σ;M) is the pointed set of 1-cocycles j:⟨σ⟩→M (j(τυ) = j(τ)·τ(j(υ))) modulo coboundaries (j ~ j' iff j'(τ) = x^{-1} j(τ) τ(x) for some x ∈ M), pointed by the trivial cocycle. Evaluation at σ identifies it with the set of m ∈ M such that m·σ(m)···σ^{p-1}(m) = 1, modulo σ-twisted conjugacy m ~ x m σ(x)^{-1}; equivalently with the set of elements mσ of the coset Mσ ⊂ M⋊⟨σ⟩ with (mσ)^p = 1, modulo conjugation by M.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.2; published version: §2.2 (Nonabelian cohomology), p. 184
items.note: Mathlib has H^1 of a group with coefficients in a module; the nonabelian (pointed-set) version for a possibly nonabelian M, with the twisted-conjugacy description, is not in the libraries. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The third description drops the cocycle condition: H^1(σ;M) is not 'elements of M modulo σ-twisted conjugacy' but the elements m = j(σ) satisfying m·σ(m)···σ^{p-1}(m) = 1 (equivalently (mσ)^p = 1 in M⋊⟨σ⟩), modulo m ~ x m σ(x)^{-1}. The paper's 'elements j(σ) ∈ M up to twisted conjugacy' carries the condition implicitly (j is a cocycle). Review note: Statement identical in both versions. 'missing' confirmed: the only nonabelian-H^1 planning in the atlas is torsor-valued H^1 of unipotent groups in AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.3 and a prerequisite remark in the upstream EllipticCurves Layer 7; neither covers a finite cyclic group acting on an abstract group.

items.name: Exact sequence of nonabelian cohomology for a σ-stable subgroup
items.statement: For σ of order p acting on M and N ⊂ M a σ-stable subgroup there is an exact sequence of pointed sets N^σ ↪ M^σ → (M/N)^σ → H^1(σ;N) → H^1(σ;M).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.2; published version: §2.2 (Nonabelian cohomology), the displayed 'long exact sequence', p. 184 (citing Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne, §§I.5.4–I.5.5)
items.note: Quoted from Serre, Galois cohomology, §§I.5.4–I.5.5. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. (M/N)^σ is the pointed set of σ-fixed cosets; exactness is in the sense of pointed sets.

items.name: Prime-to-p nilpotent normal subgroups do not change H^1
items.statement: If N ⊂ M is a σ-stable normal subgroup which is finite, nilpotent and of order prime to p, then the map H^1(σ;M) → H^1(σ;M/N) induced by M → M/N is a bijection.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.2; published version: §2.2 (Nonabelian cohomology), p. 184
items.note: Used to prove that H^1(σ,K) is finite for K virtually prime-to-p (§4.1(b)) and in the proof of Proposition 5.6. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits that N is σ-stable (needed for H^1(σ;M/N) to make sense; the paper's preceding sentence assumes it) and that N is finite ('of order prime to p'). Review note: Statement identical in both versions. Two remarks for the formaliser: (a) for finite N the nilpotency hypothesis is superfluous (Schur–Zassenhaus with the cyclic group ⟨σ⟩); (b) the consumer, §4.1(b) (published p. 191: 'In particular, H^1(σ, K) is finite (Section 2.2)'), applies it to a finite-index subgroup K' that is a projective limit of prime-to-p finite groups, i.e. to a profinite N (after replacing K' by a σ-stable normal finite-index subgroup), which §2.2 does not literally cover; the node should state the pro-(prime-to-p) version.

items.name: Level structure for a reductive group over a number field
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over a number field F and G_v = G(F_v). For v finite, K_v denotes an open compact subgroup of G_v; for v archimedean, a maximal compact subgroup of G_v; K_∞ is a maximal compact subgroup of G_∞ = G(F_∞). A level structure is an open compact subgroup K ⊂ G(A_f) of the form ∏_v K_v; for almost all v, K_v is the group of O_v-points of an integral model of G over O_F (hence hyperspecial for almost all v). For a fixed level and a set V of places, G_V = ∏'_{v∈V} G_v = {(g_v)_{v∈V} : g_v ∈ K_v for all but finitely many v}; for V a set of finite places, K_V = ∏_{w∈V} K_w and K^(V) = K_∞ ∏_{w∉V} K_w, the product over the finite places w ∉ V (2.3.1).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.3; published version: §2.3 (Algebraic groups and level structures), pp. 184–185, including (2.3.1)
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups plans adelic points, level maps and their restricted-product structure; ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces consumes them at finite level. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: Minor omissions: K_V and K^(V) are defined only for V a set of finite places; K_v at an archimedean v is a maximal compact subgroup of G_v and K_∞ a maximal compact subgroup of G_∞ = G(F_∞); G_V is the restricted product with respect to the K_v of the fixed level. The paper says K_v is a 'standard' maximal compact (O_v-points of an integral model over O_F) for almost all v; 'hyperspecial' is a true strengthening for almost all v, not the paper's wording. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. Planned citations are reasonable; AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.0 (restricted products of locally compact groups, compact-open cylinders) should be added for G_V.

items.name: The canonical torus of a reductive group
items.statement: For G connected reductive over a field F, T_can^G is the canonical F-torus of Deligne–Lusztig §1.1: for G quasisplit, the limit lim B/R_u(B) over the F-rational Borel subgroups B of G of their quotient tori (with the canonical transition isomorphisms); in general, the descent of this torus from an extension over which G is quasisplit, so that there need be no F-rational inclusion of T_can^G into G. The permutation action of Γ_F on the simple roots defines an étale F-algebra E. If G is adjoint (respectively simply connected), X^*(T_can^G) is the permutation Γ_F-module on the simple roots (respectively on the fundamental weights, permuted in the same way), so T_can^G ≅ R_{E/F} G_m and T_can^G(F) = E^×; for other semisimple G this fails.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.4; published version: §2.4 (Canonical torus), p. 185
items.note: Followed from Deligne–Lusztig §1.1. The Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap plans Borel subgroups, maximal tori and the absolute root datum with its Galois action, but not this canonical F-torus, which is what carries the global pseudoroot of §7.5. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The last clause, copied from the paper ('if G is semisimple, the F-rational points of T_can^G are naturally identified with the units in this algebra'), is false for general semisimple G; it holds when X^*(T_can^G) is the permutation module on the simple roots or on the fundamental weights, i.e. for G adjoint or simply connected. Counterexample: the quasi-split non-split SO_4, e.g. SO(3,1) over R: T_can(R) = R^× × S^1 while the étale algebra of the (swapped) simple roots is C with units C^× (see issue list). Review note: Wording otherwise identical in both versions. The false clause is not used later (published §9 defines global pseudoroots as idele class characters of T_can^G directly), so only the item needs the correction. 'missing' confirmed: no atlas stage mentions the canonical (abstract) torus.

items.name: The based root datum and the Galois action on it
items.statement: The character lattice X^* of T_can^G ×_F F-bar and its dual X_* support a canonical based root datum Ψ(G), and automorphisms of F-bar/F induce θ_G:Γ_F → Aut(Ψ(G)) ⊂ Aut(X^*). If α is a root of Ψ(G) the corresponding coroot of G-hat is written α_*, and dually α^∨_* for the root of G-hat attached to a coroot α^∨ of Ψ(G).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.4; and §2.5; published version: §2.4 (Canonical torus) and §2.5 (Dual groups and L-groups), p. 185
items.note: Layer 7 of the Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap plans the root datum of (G,T) with its Weyl group in the split case and then the absolute root datum with Galois action and the relative root system for nonsplit groups. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. Planned citation (upstream ReductiveGroups Layer 7: absolute root datum with Galois action) is apt; the based root datum of T_can itself depends on item 7.

items.name: The dual group over k and its pinning
items.statement: The dual root datum of Ψ(G) determines a pinned reductive group (G-hat, T-hat, B-hat, {X_i}) over k; the pinning splits Out(G-hat) → Aut(G-hat) and identifies Out(G-hat) with Aut(Ψ(G)). The construction is defined over F_p, so G-hat carries a Frobenius endomorphism Frob defined over k.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.5; published version: §2.5 (Dual groups and L-groups), p. 185
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 plans the pinned split dual group over Z from the dual root datum with its pinning and change-of-pinning equivalence; TV16 works with its base change to k, in characteristic p, where the Frobenius endomorphism is available. Review note: Statement identical in both versions; RG2.5 citation is apt (base change of the pinned dual group over Z to k).

items.name: The L-group as an algebraic group over k
items.statement: ^LG = G-hat ⋊ Γ_F, formed from the functorial action Γ_F → Out(G-hat) ⊂ Aut(G-hat), regarded as an algebraic group over k with infinite component group. A morphism ^LH → ^LG of such groups is determined by the induced map on k-points, but may have nontrivial scheme-theoretic fibres.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.5; published version: §2.5 (Dual groups and L-groups), pp. 185–186
items.note: RG2.5 plans the semidirect L-group with its projection and action law; the characteristic-p convention (dual groups over k rather than over C) and the remark on k-points versus schemes are the paper's own. Review note: Statement identical in both versions.

items.name: The local L-group at an unramified place
items.statement: For v a finite place at which G splits over an unramified extension of F_v, ^LG_v = G-hat ⋊ ⟨Frob_v⟩, where ⟨Frob_v⟩ is the discrete infinite cyclic group topologically generating the unramified quotient of Γ_{F_v}.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.6; published version: §2.6 (Local L-groups), p. 186
items.note: The same layer plans the L-group and its functorial data; the unramified local form is its restriction along ⟨Frob_v⟩ ⊂ Γ_{F_v}. Review note: Statement identical in both versions.

items.name: Parabolics of G, dual Levis of G-hat, and the duality L^ab ↔ Z(L-hat)
items.statement: A G(F̄)-conjugacy class of parabolic subgroups P ⊂ G ×_F F̄ determines the subset Δ_P of the simple roots of Ψ(G) consisting of the α for which −α is a root of P (for the action of T_can induced by any Borel subgroup B ⊂ P and splitting of B → T_can, all over F̄). The corresponding Levi subgroup L̂ ⊂ Ĝ is generated by T̂ and the coroot homomorphisms SL_2 → Ĝ for α ∈ Δ_P. The abelianisation L^ab of the Levi quotient L of P is dual to the torus Z(L̂)°: X^*(L^ab) = {χ ∈ X^*(T_can) : ⟨χ, α^∨⟩ = 0 for all α ∈ Δ_P}, X_*(Z(L̂)) is the orthogonal complement of {α^∨_* : α ∈ Δ_P} in X_*(T̂), and these lattices coincide under X^*(T_can) = X_*(T̂).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.7; published version: §2.7 (Parabolics and Levis in G and Ĝ), p. 186; the description of X^*(L^ab) was corrected in print
items.note: Layer 7 of the Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap plans parabolic subgroups and the Levi decomposition, and RG2.5 plans Levi inclusions in the dual group; the explicit duality between the abelianised Levi and the centre of the dual Levi is what TV16 uses to read off Satake parameters of parabolic inductions. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies the preprint's X^*(L^ab) = X^*(T_can)/⟨α^∨ : α ∈ Δ_P⟩, which is ill-typed (α^∨ lies in X_*, not X^*) and was corrected in the published version to 'those elements of X^*(T^can) trivial on ⟨α^∨ : α ∈ Δ_P⟩'. Also: P ⊂ G ×_F F̄, and L^ab is dual to the identity component Z(L̂)° (Z(L̂) can be disconnected, e.g. G = PGL_2, P = G). Review note: When G is simply connected (Ĝ adjoint) every Z(L̂) is connected, so the paper's main applications are unaffected.

items.name: Frobenius endomorphism of a k-group with an F_p-descent
items.statement: For any k-group scheme equipped with a descent to F_p, Frob denotes its Frobenius endomorphism; for G-hat the fixed point subgroup of Frob is the discrete set of F_p-points of G-hat.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.8; published version: §2.8 (Frobenius maps), p. 186
items.note: Layer 9 of the Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap plans pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over Z, their base change to any k and their points over an algebraically closed field functorially in the field, so that a field endomorphism — the q-power Frobenius first of all — induces a group endomorphism. Review note: Statement identical in both versions.

items.name: Unramified characters of a torus and their Langlands parameters
items.statement: Let T be a torus over a number field F, unramified at a finite place v (T_v = T(F_v) splits over an unramified extension of F_v), let A_v ⊂ T be the maximal F_v-split subtorus and A_v = A_v(F_v). A homomorphism T_v → k^× is unramified if it is trivial on the maximal compact subgroup of T_v. Then (i) restriction is a bijection from unramified characters of T_v to unramified characters of A_v (2.9.1); (ii) the surjection T̂ → Â_v identifies Â_v with the Frob_v-coinvariants T̂_{Frob_v}, so unramified characters χ of T_v correspond bijectively to elements of T̂_{Frob_v}(k), equivalently to T̂(k)-conjugacy classes of splittings ⟨Frob_v⟩ → ^LT̂_v = T̂ ⋊ ⟨Frob_v⟩; either is called the Langlands parameter of χ; (iii) since X^*(T)^{Frob_v} → X^*(A_v) is injective with finite cokernel and k^× is divisible, X^*(T)^{Frob_v} ⊗ k^× → X^*(A_v) ⊗ k^× is surjective, so every unramified χ comes (possibly not uniquely) from an element of X^*(T)^{Frob_v} ⊗ k^×, where α ⊗ λ gives t ↦ λ^{v(α(t))}; (iv) if t_χ ∈ T̂(k) is the image of such an element under X^*(T) ⊗ k^× = X_*(T̂) ⊗ k^× = T̂(k) (2.9.2), then χ is parametrised by the splitting Frob_v ↦ t_χ Frob_v.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.9; published version: §2.9 (Class field theory), pp. 186–187, (2.9.1) and (2.9.2)
items.note: The Langlands correspondence for unramified tori with k^*-coefficients. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 plans identifying Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters, but no layer plans the torus case itself. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: (1) Unramified characters of T_v are in bijection with T̂_{Frob_v}(k) = Â_v(k), i.e. Frob_v-twisted conjugacy classes in T̂(k), not with elements t_χ ∈ T̂(k); t_χ is a representative. (2) The explicit formula t ↦ λ^{v(α(t))} requires α ∈ X^*(T)^{Frob_v} (an F_v-rational character), and X^*(T)^{Frob_v} ⊗ k^× → X^*(A_v) ⊗ k^× is only surjective, so every unramified character arises, not necessarily uniquely. Change in print: the published version calls both the element of T̂_{Frob_v} and the splitting ⟨Frob_v⟩ → ^LT̂_v the 'Langlands parameter' of χ (the preprint names only the element). Review note: 'missing' confirmed: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 plans eigencharacters versus unramified parameters for unramified G, and no stage plans the torus case with k^×-coefficients.

items.name: The Hecke algebra Fun_G(S×S) of a discrete G-set
items.statement: Let G be a locally compact totally disconnected group and S a discrete set with a continuous left G-action whose stabilisers are compact (hence compact open). Fun_G(S×S) is the k-vector space of G-invariant functions h: S×S → k supported on finitely many G-orbits; it is an algebra under (h_1∗h_2)(x,z) = Σ_{y∈S} h_1(x,y)h_2(y,z) (2.10.1), the sums being finite. It acts on the left on k[S] by h∗s = Σ_{t∈S} h(t,s)t. If S has finitely many G-orbits, Fun_G(S×S) has a unit and this action identifies it with End_G(k[S]).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.10; published version: §2.10 (Hecke algebras), p. 187, (2.10.1) and the action on k[S]
items.note: The double-coset special case S = G/K is in the libraries (see the next item); this general S-version, which TV16 needs for the set of singular simplices in X, is not. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: With the multiplication (2.10.1), the printed action h∗s = Σ_t h(s,t)t (copied into the item) is a right action: h_1∗(h_2∗s) = (h_2∗h_1)∗s. The left action is h∗s = Σ_t h(t,s)t, and it is this one that gives, by precomposition, the right module structure (2.10.2) on V^K (see issues). The item's note is also inaccurate: §2.11 does not use Fun_G(S×S) for S = Hom(Δ^m,X); it uses the right H(G,K)-action (2.10.3) on a right G-set. The general S is used only to define H(G,K) = Fun_G(G/K × G/K). Review note: Statement identical in both versions. Route 3 (SR.1) is a reasonable home, but SR.1 plans convolution of compactly supported functions with idempotents e_U when indices are invertible, not the Fun_G(S×S) formalism in characteristic p.

items.name: The spherical Hecke algebra H(G,K) and its anti-involution
items.statement: For K ⊂ G compact open, H(G,K) = Fun_G(G/K × G/K) is identified with the finitely supported functions on K\G/K by h(K,gK) = h(KgK); H(G,K;F_q) is the subalgebra of F_q-valued functions. The anti-involution KgK ↦ Kg^{-1}K exchanges left and right H(G,K)-modules. For a left G-module V over k, V^K = Hom_G(k[G/K],V) is a right H(G,K)-module by v∗h = Σ_{Kg∈K\G} g^{-1}v h(K,gK) = Σ_{gK∈G/K} h(gK,K) g v. For a set X with a right G-action, k[X/K] is a right H(G,K)-module by xK∗h = Σ_{gK∈G/K} xgK h(K,gK) (2.10.3).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.10; published version: §2.10 (Hecke algebras), pp. 187–188, (2.10.2)–(2.10.3)
items.note: Mathlib's IsHeckeTriple/HeckeRing and the Tau Ceti Hecke-ring files give the double-coset algebra with its convolution, associativity, the anti-involution and the commutativity criterion it yields; TV16 uses it with k-coefficients. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: Formula (2.10.2), copied into the item, is not well defined: replacing g by gk changes g^{-1}v to k^{-1}g^{-1}v. It should sum over Kg ∈ K\G, or equivalently read v∗h = Σ_{gK∈G/K} h(gK,K) g v. Also, the identification k[X/K] ≃ k[X]^K used with (2.10.3) holds only when the K-orbits on X are finite; (2.10.3) itself is well defined on k[X/K] for any right G-set X. Review note: Library citations confirmed: Mathlib IsHeckeTriple, HeckeRing (NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean:189), HeckeCosetModule; Tau Ceti HeckeCosetModule.instRingHeckeRing (NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Associativity.lean:485), HeckeAntiInvolution.bar (Commutativity.lean:98), HeckeCosetModule.commSemiringOfAntiInvolution (Commutativity.lean:478). They cover the double-coset algebra and the anti-involution only. Neither library has the right module structures on V^K and k[X/K]. SR.1 plans e_U-corner modules only when the index denominators are invertible, which excludes the characteristic-p case the paper needs. So the status is library only for the algebra: split off the two module structures as a missing construction (route 1, which consumes them in §§2.11 and 4).

items.name: X is the inverse limit of its finite-level quotients
items.statement: Let G be a locally compact totally disconnected group, K ⊂ G a compact open (hence profinite) subgroup, and X a locally compact Hausdorff space with a continuous right G-action whose restriction to K is free and proper. If K_1 ⊃ K_2 ⊃ ⋯ are open normal subgroups of K with ∩_n K_n = {e} (more generally, a directed family of such subgroups with trivial intersection), then the natural map π: X → lim_n X/K_n is a homeomorphism (2.11.1).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.11; published version: §2.11 (Hecke actions on homology and cohomology), p. 188, (2.11.1) and the proof after it
items.note: The proof given is an explicit closed-map argument using compact neighbourhoods; it is the step that makes every singular simplex of X/K lift to X uniquely up to K. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The family {K_i} must be directed (in practice a decreasing sequence K_1 ⊃ K_2 ⊃ …, as the index n in lim X/K_n suggests). For an arbitrary collection with trivial intersection, the limit over the collection ordered by inclusion can be strictly larger than X (see issues). Also make explicit that G is locally compact totally disconnected, so K is profinite. Review note: Statement and proof identical in both versions.

items.name: Hecke action on the homology and cohomology of X/K
items.statement: With G, K, X as in the previous item, the set Hom(Δ^m,X) of singular m-simplices is a right G-set on which K acts freely, and Hom(Δ^m,X)/K is the set of singular m-simplices of X/K: each simplex of X/K lifts to X, uniquely up to K, by the previous item and the coverings X/K_n → X/K. Formula (2.10.3), applied to the right G-set Hom(Δ^m,X), defines a right H(G,K)-action on C_m(X/K;k) = k[Hom(Δ^m,X)/K] (= the K-coinvariants of k[Hom(Δ^m,X)]) that commutes with the face maps. It descends to a right action on H_m(X/K;k), and the duality H^m(X/K;k) = Hom_k(H_m(X/K;k),k) turns it into a left action on H^m(X/K;k).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.11; published version: §2.11 (Hecke actions on homology and cohomology), pp. 188–189
items.note: ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces plans local systems and chain complexes at finite level (ALS.1) and Hecke correspondences on those complexes with their coherence data (ALS.3); this is that action, written through the double-coset algebra. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item's 'Fun_G acting on k[Hom(Δ^m,X)]^K' follows a slip in the paper. The action used is the right H(G,K)-action (2.10.3) with the right G-set Hom(Δ^m,X) in place of X. The paper writes 'with S = Hom(Δ^m,X)', and C_m(X/K) = k[Hom(Δ^m,X)/K] is the coinvariants k[Hom(Δ^m,X)]_K. The printed k[Hom(Δ^m,X)]^K is 0 when K is infinite, because the free K-orbits are infinite. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. The planned citations are reasonable, but ALS.3 builds Hecke operators as correspondences through K ∩ gKg^{-1} (pullback and trace), not by this singular-simplex construction. The node needs the comparison between the two, since Theorem 4.4 (route 1) uses the chain-level action on singular chains.

items.name: Borel–de Siebenthal subgroups for an inner automorphism of order p
items.statement: Let G be simply connected over F-bar with B_G ⊃ T, simple roots {α_i}, highest root α_0 and fundamental coweights ω_i^∨. If ⟨ω_i^∨,α_0⟩ = p then there is a unique connected semisimple H ⊂ G containing T such that -α_0 and the α_j (j ≠ i) are roots of T on H while α_i is not, and Δ(H) = {-α_0} ∪ {α_j}_{j≠i} is a system of simple roots for H, realised by deleting vertex i from the extended Dynkin diagram of G.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.12, the unnumbered Theorem; not in the published version
items.note: H is the centraliser of a representative s ∈ T of ω_i^∨(ζ) for ζ a primitive p-th root of unity; Z(H)/Z(G) then has an element of order p. Automorphisms of the extended Dynkin diagram permute the ω_i^∨ with ⟨ω_i^∨,α_0⟩ = p and conjugate the corresponding H, so this lists the G(F-bar)-conjugacy classes of order-p inner automorphisms with semisimple fixed points. Review note: Not in the published version: §§2.12–2.13 were removed together with the preprint's §§9–12 case-by-case proof. The published text refers to this material only indirectly: §1.3, p. 181 ('Using Theorem 8.10 and case by case arguments, we have verified that a σ-dual homomorphism exists whenever G is simply connected and H is semisimple — with three possible exceptions when G has type E6. … Details will appear elsewhere; roughly speaking, we can treat many inner cases at once by the general methods of Section 9.7'), and §9 preamble, p. 220 ('we have in fact carried out such computations in some generality, but here we will give only examples'). Keep this item only if the preprint's proof of the Second Main Theorem (item 82 and the §§9–12 case analysis) is kept as a preprint-only route; otherwise drop it together with that route. The item's statement is right. It silently fixes two preprint misprints (ω_i^∨ is called a 'fundamental weight', and part (1) omits j ≠ i; see issues). The preprint's later reference '§2.12(3)' (TeX line 3948, in §10) points to a part (3) that does not exist; the fact it needs, that the root lattice of G has index p over that of H, belongs in this item.

items.name: Endoscopic subgroups of the dual group
items.statement: Let G be simply connected, Ĝ its dual group over k (characteristic p) with pinned maximal torus and Borel T̂_G ⊂ B̂_G, simple roots {α^∨_{i,*}}, α^∨_{0,*} the highest short root of Ĝ and α_{i,*}, α_{0,*} the corresponding coroots (α_{0,*} is the highest coroot of Ĝ and corresponds to the highest root α_0 of G). If the coefficient ⟨ω^∨_{i,*},α_{0,*}⟩ of α_{i,*} in α_{0,*} equals p, there is a unique connected semisimple smooth subgroup Ĥ_0 ⊂ Ĝ containing T̂_G such that −α^∨_{0,*} and the α^∨_{j,*} (j ≠ i) are roots of T̂_G on Ĥ_0, α^∨_{i,*} is not, and {−α^∨_{0,*}} ∪ {α^∨_{j,*}}_{j≠i} is a system of simple roots of Ĥ_0 (delete α^∨_{i,*} from the diagram on {α^∨_{j,*}} ∪ {−α^∨_{0,*}}). Its roots are the α^∨_* for α a root of the Borel–de Siebenthal subgroup H of item 19.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.13, the unnumbered Theorem (label DTT2); not in the published version
items.note: These are the full-rank semisimple subgroups of G-hat not captured by Borel–de Siebenthal, arising in duality with centralisers in G; the paper calls them endoscopic subgroups, and they appear on the Galois side. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The setting is missing: Ĝ is over k of characteristic p and is the dual of a simply connected G. The condition ⟨ω^∨_{i,*},α_{0,*}⟩ = p is the same as the Borel–de Siebenthal condition ⟨ω_i^∨,α_0⟩ = p of item 19, because α_{0,*} is the coroot of Ĝ attached to the highest root α_0 of G. 'The extended Dynkin diagram of Ĝ' here means the diagram of {α^∨_{j,*}} ∪ {−α^∨_{0,*}} with α^∨_{0,*} the highest short root. That is the dual of G's extended diagram, which differs from Ĝ's usual extended diagram when G is not simply laced. Review note: Not in the published version: §§2.12–2.13 were removed together with the preprint's §§9–12 case-by-case proof. The published text refers to this material only indirectly: §1.3, p. 181 ('Using Theorem 8.10 and case by case arguments, we have verified that a σ-dual homomorphism exists whenever G is simply connected and H is semisimple — with three possible exceptions when G has type E6. … Details will appear elsewhere; roughly speaking, we can treat many inner cases at once by the general methods of Section 9.7'), and §9 preamble, p. 220 ('we have in fact carried out such computations in some generality, but here we will give only examples'). Keep this item only if the preprint's proof of the Second Main Theorem (item 82 and the §§9–12 case analysis) is kept as a preprint-only route; otherwise drop it together with that route. The preprint's 'thus α^∨_{0,*} is the highest coroot of Ĝ' is a misprint for α_{0,*} (see issues). The item avoids it.

items.name: Quasi-closed sets of roots and the duality of Borel–de Siebenthal data
items.statement: A smooth connected subgroup scheme of G (or Ĝ) containing a split maximal torus T is determined by its set S of roots with respect to T, and the sets that occur are exactly the quasi-closed ones. For root systems not of type G_2: S is quasi-closed iff, whenever α, β ∈ S and i, j > 0 with iα + jβ a root whose commutator coefficient N_{αβ,ij} is not divisible by p, iα + jβ ∈ S. For symmetric S (S = −S), this is equivalent to the following. For α, β ∈ S spanning the rank-2 subsystem Ψ = Φ ∩ (Qα + Qβ), Ψ ∩ S is Ψ, or the long roots of Ψ, or (possible only when p = 2) the short roots of Ψ. If S is the root set of the Borel–de Siebenthal subgroup H of item 19, then {α^∨_* : α ∈ S} is quasi-closed in Ĝ over k. This is automatic when G is simply laced or p = 2, and it is checked by hand for F_4 and G_2 with p = 3.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §2.13; the proof of the unnumbered Theorem; not in the published version
items.note: This is the proof of the previous item. It is automatic for G simply laced or p = 2; the remaining cases F_4 and G_2 with p = 3 are checked by hand. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: 'A smooth subgroup scheme … corresponds to a quasi-closed subset S of roots' needs 'connected' and 'containing the split maximal torus' (Borel–Tits §3; Sopkina, Cor. 5, as cited). Also say what 'root subsystem spanned by two elements' means. Review note: Not in the published version: §§2.12–2.13 were removed together with the preprint's §§9–12 case-by-case proof. The published text refers to this material only indirectly: §1.3, p. 181 ('Using Theorem 8.10 and case by case arguments, we have verified that a σ-dual homomorphism exists whenever G is simply connected and H is semisimple — with three possible exceptions when G has type E6. … Details will appear elsewhere; roughly speaking, we can treat many inner cases at once by the general methods of Section 9.7'), and §9 preamble, p. 220 ('we have in fact carried out such computations in some generality, but here we will give only examples'). Keep this item only if the preprint's proof of the Second Main Theorem (item 82 and the §§9–12 case analysis) is kept as a preprint-only route; otherwise drop it together with that route.

items.name: Tate cohomology of a Z/p-module
items.statement: For M an abelian group with an action of the cyclic group ⟨σ⟩ of order p, T^0(M) = ker(1-σ)/im(N) and T^1(M) = ker(N)/im(1-σ), with N = 1+σ+···+σ^{p-1}; these are the cohomology of the 2-periodic complex whose differentials alternate between 1-σ and N, so each short exact sequence of σ-modules gives a six-term exact sequence T^0(M') → T^0(M) → T^0(M'') → T^1(M') → T^1(M) → T^1(M'') → T^0(M').
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §3.1; published version: §3.1 (Definition of Tate cohomology), p. 189
items.note: Mathlib has the Tate complex and Tate cohomology of a finite group together with the connecting map and the long exact sequence of a short exact sequence; Tau Ceti identifies degree 0 with M^G/NM, degree -1 with ker N/I_G M, and proves 2-periodicity for a cyclic group, so T^0 and T^1 here are Tate cohomology in degrees 0 and -1. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. Library citations confirmed at the pinned commits. Mathlib: tateCohomology (RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean:145), Rep.tateNorm (:63), TateCohomology.δ (:200), exact₁ (:217), exact₃ (:213); middle exactness comes from homology_exact₂ of map_tateComplexFunctor_shortExact and has no named lemma. Tau Ceti: TauCeti.TateCohomology.H0IsoNormQuotient (LowDegree.lean:88), HNegOneIsoNormKernelQuotient (:181), Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.periodicIso (Periodic.lean:341). T^0 = Ĥ^0 and T^1 = Ĥ^{-1}. The hexagon's map T^0(M'') → T^1(M') is δ followed by the periodicity isomorphism Ĥ^1 ≅ Ĥ^{-1}, which depends on the generator σ.

items.name: Tate cohomology of smooth compactly supported functions on an l-space
items.statement: Let X be an l-space (Hausdorff, locally compact, totally disconnected) with a continuous action of σ of order p. Restriction to fixed points induces isomorphisms T^i(C_c^∞(X;k)) → C_c^∞(X^σ;k) for i = 0,1; restriction followed by reduction mod p gives an isomorphism T^0(C_c^∞(X;W)) → C_c^∞(X^σ;k), and T^1(C_c^∞(X;W)) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §3.2; published version: §3.2 (Tate on smooth functions on ℓ-spaces), statements (1)–(2), p. 189
items.note: The special case of the sheaf statement below, for the constant sheaf; the W-coefficient statement is what makes Tate cohomology behave like a mod p localisation. Review note: Statement identical in both versions, apart from 'give'→'given'. Write Λ for W(k), as in both versions.

items.name: Tate cohomology of sections commutes with Tate cohomology of the sheaf
items.statement: Let X be an l-space with a continuous σ-action of order p and F a σ-equivariant sheaf of k- or W-modules on X. Restricting compactly supported sections to X^σ induces an isomorphism T^i(Γ_c(X;F)) → Γ_c(X^σ;T^i(F|_{X^σ})) for i = 0,1, where T^i(F|_{X^σ}) is the sheaf ker(1-σ)/im(N), respectively ker(N)/im(1-σ), on X^σ.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §3.3; the unnumbered Proposition; published version: §3.3 (Tate on sheaves on ℓ-spaces), the unnumbered Proposition ('The map (3.3.1) is an isomorphism'), pp. 189–190
items.note: Proved by the short exact sequence 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 with F'' supported on X^σ and F' vanishing along X^σ, exactness of Γ_c, and the vanishing of T^i(Γ_c(U;F')) when U^σ is empty. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. In the proof, the σ-invariant compact U' must be compact open (see issues).

items.name: Existence of fundamental domains for a free action on a compact l-space
items.statement: If σ of order p acts freely on a compact l-space X, there is a closed and open F ⊂ X such that X is the disjoint union of the σ^i F for 0 ≤ i ≤ p-1.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §3.3; in the proof of the unnumbered Proposition; published version: §3.3, 'existence of fundamental domains', stated and proved just before the proof of the Proposition, p. 190
items.note: Constructed from a finite cover by clopen sets U_i with σ(U_i)∩U_i empty, by passing to the algebra of sets they generate and choosing orbit representatives among its minimal nonempty elements. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. The argument checks out for every prime p: each block B of the partition is disjoint from σB, and σ^jB = B would force σB = B.

items.name: Tate cohomology of a ring and extension of characters
items.statement: If A is a commutative unital k-algebra with a σ-action of order p, then NA is an ideal of A^σ, so A-bar = T^0 A = A^σ/NA is a ring, and restriction of characters is a bijection Hom(A,k)^σ → Hom(A-bar,k). More generally, for B a commutative integral domain, every χ:A-bar → B has the property that χ^p extends uniquely to A.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §3.4; published version: §3.4 (Tate on rings), (3.4.1) with its proof and the closing remark on integral domains, pp. 190–191
items.note: The inverse sends χ to a ↦ χ(a a^σ ··· a^{σ^{p-1}})^{1/p}; uniqueness uses the linear independence of characters, which the libraries have as linearIndependent_monoidHom. This is the algebraic engine behind the normalized Brauer homomorphism. Review note: Statement identical in both versions. σ acts by k-algebra automorphisms and Hom(A,k) means k-algebra homomorphisms. In the integral-domain version, 'χ^p extends uniquely' means that χ∘Nm, with Nm(a) = a·σ(a)···σ^{p-1}(a) mod NA, is the unique ring homomorphism A → B restricting to χ^p on A^σ. The consumer is §4.3 (published p. 193), which uses it to define the normalized Brauer homomorphism. Mathlib's linearIndependent_monoidHom (LinearAlgebra/LinearIndependent/Basic.lean:502) applies directly over an integral domain, so no passage to the fraction field is needed. Stray 'χ̃_1' misprint: see issues.

items.name: σ-plain open compact subgroups
items.statement: Let G be locally compact totally disconnected with an action of σ with σ^p = 1, and K ⊂ G open compact with σ(K) = K. K is σ-plain if (a) G^σ/K^σ → (G/K)^σ is a bijection — equivalently G^σ acts transitively on (G/K)^σ, equivalently H^1(σ,K) → H^1(σ,G) has trivial fibre over the trivial class — and (b) K is virtually prime-to-p, i.e. contains a finite index subgroup that is a projective limit of finite groups of order prime to p, so that H^1(σ,K) is finite.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.1 (preprint p. 12); published version: §4.1 (σ-actions, σ-plain subgroups; the definition of σ-plain, conditions (a) and (b)), p. 191
items.note: This is the technical hypothesis under which the Brauer homomorphism is defined and behaves; it is verified at almost all places in Proposition 5.6. Review note: Same text in both versions. Status missing is right: nothing in the atlas or the libraries mentions σ-plain subgroups or the nonabelian H^1(σ, K) used here.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism of Hecke algebras
items.statement: For K ⊂ G σ-plain, restriction of h from G/K×G/K to (G/K)^σ×(G/K)^σ = G^σ/K^σ×G^σ/K^σ defines Br: H(G,K)^σ → H(G^σ,K^σ), and Br is an algebra homomorphism because the summands of the convolution are permuted by σ and k has characteristic p.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.2 (preprint pp. 12–13); published version: §4.2 (The Brauer homomorphism; the definition of Br), pp. 191–192
items.note: The analogue for modular representations of finite groups is the classical Brauer homomorphism; nothing in the atlas plans either version. Review note: Same in both versions. Status missing is right (no layer plans a Brauer homomorphism of Hecke algebras).

items.name: Compatibility of the Brauer homomorphism with Tate cohomology of permutation modules
items.statement: For σ acting on a set S there are canonical identifications ker(1-σ)/im(N) = k[S^σ] and ker(N)/im(1-σ) = k[S^σ]. If S-tilde is a right G-set with compatible σ-action on which K acts freely and S = S-tilde/K, then k[S-tilde^σ/K^σ] is an H(G,K)^σ-direct summand of k[S^σ] = T^i k[S] and the action of T^i h on it coincides with Br(h), for i = 0 and i = 1.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.2, (4.2.1) and (4.2.2) (preprint p. 13); published version: §4.2, (4.2.1) and (4.2.2) with the argument after them, pp. 192–193
items.note: The summand statement uses the nondegenerate pairing on k[S^σ] and the anti-involution of the Hecke algebra; the identification of the action uses that σ acts freely on G/K minus (G/K)^σ, which is exactly σ-plainness. Review note: Statement matches. The published text adds two remarks: (4.2.1) is Proposition 3.3 for the constant sheaf, and H(G,K)^σ acts on k[S^σ] ≃ T^0 k[S] through the quotient H(G,K)^σ → T^0(H(G,K)). The library has the carrier, but not this result. Mathlib 082e2d3 has `tateCohomology` (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean). Tau Ceti f790474 has `Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.tateCohomologyIso₀` and `tateCohomologyIsoNegOne` (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Periodic.lean), which identify Ĥ^0 = ker(1−σ)/im N and Ĥ^{−1} = ker N/im(1−σ) for a cyclic group, i.e. the paper's T^0 and T^1. Neither library computes T^i of a permutation module as k[S^σ] or has the Hecke statement, so the status stays missing; cite these declarations as the carrier.

items.name: The normalized Brauer homomorphism
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G be σ-plain, and suppose H(G,K) and H(G^σ,K^σ) are commutative integral domains. Br: H(G,K)^σ → H(G^σ,K^σ) kills N·H(G,K), so it factors through T^0 H(G,K). By §3.4 the map Br~(h) := Br(h ∗ h^σ ∗ ⋯ ∗ h^{σ^{p−1}}) is the unique ring homomorphism H(G,K) → H(G^σ,K^σ) that extends Br^p from H(G,K)^σ, and it is Frobenius-semilinear. The normalized Brauer homomorphism br: H(G,K) → H(G^σ,K^σ) is the unique k-linear map that agrees with Br~ on the F_p-structure Fun_G(G/K×G/K; F_p). It is a k-algebra homomorphism, and explicitly br(h)(K^σ, gK^σ) = ((h ∗ h^σ ∗ ⋯ ∗ h^{σ^{p−1}})(K, gK))^{1/p} for g ∈ G^σ. This reduces to the printed ((h∗⋯∗h)(K,gK))^{1/p} (p-fold convolution) only when h is σ-invariant.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.3, including the displayed formula (4.3.1) (preprint p. 13); published version: §4.3 (Normalized Brauer homomorphism), (4.3.1), p. 193
items.note: The p-th power and the 1/p-th root are what force characteristic p and make the Satake parameter of the transfer a p-th power (see the Theorem of §8.1). Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The explicit formula is copied from (4.3.1), which is wrong for h that are not σ-invariant (both versions; see the new issue on (4.3.1)). The p-fold self-convolution h∗⋯∗h must be the norm product h∗h^σ∗⋯∗h^{σ^{p−1}}. The item also leaves implicit that K is σ-plain, which Br needs. Review note: Status missing is right. Downstream, the published §8.15 (p. 219) uses br only through its definition (the linear extension of Br^p from the F_p-valued algebra and uniqueness of extensions), never through (4.3.1).

items.name: Smith theory for Hecke modules (Theorem 4.4(a))
items.statement: Let G,K,X be as in §2.11, with σ acting compatibly on G,K,X so that G^σ,K^σ,X^σ again satisfy those conditions, X/K of finite cohomological dimension and K σ-plain. Regard H^*(X/K) and H^*(X^σ/K^σ) as H(G,K)^σ-modules, the first by restriction and the second through Br. Then every composition factor of H^*(X^σ/K^σ) is a composition factor of H^*(X/K).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Theorem 4.4(a) (preprint p. 13; proof pp. 14–15); published version: Theorem 4.4(a), p. 193, with proof pp. 194–196
items.note: The main local-to-global mechanism of the paper: fixed-point localisation in the sense of Smith, Borel and Quillen, kept Hecke-equivariant. Review note: The statement matches the published text word for word. The proof has a gap in step (3), the convergence of the vh spectral sequence for the unbounded singular chain complex (new issue). The proof actually shows more than (a): H_*(X^σ/K^σ) is a subquotient of T^*H_*(X/K). That stronger form is what Theorem 6.5 uses, so it is proposed as a new item under coverage. Status missing is right.

items.name: Smith theory for Hecke eigenvalues (Theorem 4.4(b))
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 4.4, suppose also that H(G,K) and H(G^σ,K^σ) are commutative integral domains (so br is defined) and that H^*(X/K) is finite-dimensional over k. If χ: H(G^σ,K^σ) → k is a character with a nonzero eigenvector in H^*(X^σ/K^σ), then χ∘br: H(G,K) → k has a nonzero eigenvector in H^*(X/K). Without the finiteness hypothesis, the argument shows only that χ∘Br is an H(G,K)^σ-composition factor of H^*(X/K).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Theorem 4.4(b) (preprint p. 13; the deduction (a) ⇒ (b) on p. 14); published version: Theorem 4.4(b), p. 193, with the deduction from (a) via (4.4.3) on p. 194
items.note: Deduced from (a) together with the uniqueness of extensions of characters (§3.4) and the semilinear action of Aut(k) on the F_p-structures of H^*(X/K) and H(G,K). Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies the printed statement, but the printed deduction (a) ⇒ (b) needs a finiteness hypothesis that the theorem does not state (new issue). (a) gives χ∘Br only as a composition factor of H^*(X/K) restricted to H(G,K)^σ. Turning that into an eigenvector of H(G,K)^σ, and then of H(G,K), needs H^*(X/K) to be finite-dimensional over k, or at least needs finite-dimensional generalised eigenspaces. Review note: The added hypothesis holds where the theorem is applied: H^*([G]_K) is finite-dimensional, as the proof of Theorem 5.8 itself notes. So Theorems 5.8 and 6.5 are unaffected by this point. Status missing is right.

items.name: The Smith double complex and its two spectral sequences
items.statement: C_*^Smith is the double complex with columns indexed by i ∈ Z, each column a copy of the singular chain complex C_*(X/K), and horizontal maps alternating N and 1−σ (··· ←N− C_*(X/K) ←(1−σ)− C_*(X/K) ←N− ···). It is a double complex of H(G,K)^σ-modules. Its two spectral sequences are as follows. hvE: horizontal differential first, with hvE^1_{ij} = T^i C_j(X/K) = C_j((X/K)^σ) and hvE^2_{ij} = H_j((X/K)^σ). vhE: vertical differential first, with vhE^1_{ij} = H_j(X/K) and vhE^2_{ij} = T^i H_j(X/K). For a bounded complex in place of C_*(X/K), both converge to the homology of the total complex. With the unbounded singular complex and the direct-sum totalisation, hvE converges, because the row filtration is bounded below and exhaustive. vhE need not converge to the same homology.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.3; in the proof of Theorem 4.4 (the printed number is 4.4: the theorem shares the subsection counter, so the proof sits in §4.4 even though the TeX places it after the \subsection 'Normalized Brauer homomorphism'; preprint p. 14); published version: §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4, the Smith double complex and the two spectral sequences, p. 194 (E^1, E^2 identifications on pp. 195–196)
items.note: The recipe for lifting a form on Y to X. The paper expects the higher differentials to be nonzero and to carry arithmetic information (§1.4(iv)). Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item says both spectral sequences converge to the homology of the total complex. The source claims this only 'if C_* is bounded'. The singular chain complex C_*(X/K) used here is not bounded, and step (3)'s appeal to the vanishing of H_*(X/K) in high degrees does not repair this (new issue). Review note: The paper expects the higher differentials of vhE to be nonzero (published §1.4, p. 182, and §1.5(iii), p. 183). Status missing is right.

items.name: Degeneration of the horizontal-first spectral sequence
items.statement: In the Smith double complex, every class of hvE^2 is represented by a cycle in C_*((X/K)^σ), and hence d^r = 0 for all r ≥ 2: hvE^2 = hvE^∞.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.3; step (1) of the proof of Theorem 4.4 (printed as part of §4.4; preprint p. 14); published version: §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4, step (1) 'Degeneration of hvE', p. 195
items.note: Uses only the identification of Tate cohomology of a permutation module with the fixed-point chains. Review note: The statement is correct. The published step (1) has a misprint that the preprint lacks: ε ∈ hvE^1_{i+1,j} = C_j((X/K)^σ) where hvE^0_{i+1,j} = C_j(X/K) is meant (new issue). The argument also uses that a chain supported on σ-fixed simplices and lying in im(N) or im(1−σ) is zero.

items.name: X^σ/K^σ is a union of connected components of (X/K)^σ
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 4.4, let Y ⊂ X be the inverse image of (X/K)^σ. For y ∈ Y let κ(y) ∈ K be the unique element with yκ(y) = σ(y). κ(y) is a 1-cocycle: κ(y)σ(κ(y))⋯σ^{p−1}(κ(y)) = 1, because σ^p = 1 and K acts freely. κ: Y → K is continuous, since its graph is closed and projects homeomorphically to Y, and it is K-equivariant for σ-twisted conjugation. It therefore descends to a continuous map (X/K)^σ → H^1(σ, K), which is finite by σ-plainness (b) and discrete because each class is closed in the closed set of cocycles. The fibre over the trivial class is X^σ/K^σ. Hence X^σ/K^σ is open and closed in (X/K)^σ, i.e. a union of connected components.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §4.3; step (2) of the proof of Theorem 4.4 (printed as part of §4.4; preprint p. 15); published version: §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4, step (2) 'Compatibility with the Brauer homomorphism', p. 195
items.note: The finiteness and discreteness of the target is exactly σ-plainness together with the closedness of twisted conjugacy classes in K. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: Following the source, the item calls the target 'σ-twisted conjugacy classes' of K and says it is finite and discrete. The set of all σ-twisted conjugacy classes of K is in general infinite. What is finite, by σ-plainness (b), is H^1(σ, K), the twisted classes of 1-cocycles, and κ(y) is always a cocycle (new misprint issue). Review note: Status missing is right.

items.name: The locally symmetric space [G]_K
items.statement: For G connected reductive over F, K_∞ ⊂ G(F_∞) a maximal compact subgroup and K ⊂ G(A_f) a level structure (§2.3), [G]_K := G(F)\G(A)/(K_∞ × K). If K ∩ G(F) is torsion-free, the homology and cohomology of [G]_K (with k-coefficients) carry the action of H(G(A_f), K) of §2.11. The paper works only in this torsion-free case: for general K one would regard [G]_K as an orbifold, and the paper does not use that.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Definition 5.1 (preprint p. 15); published version: §5.1 (Definition), p. 196
items.note: ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.0 plans the symmetric space and the finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic components with explicit stabilizers, and neat-level freeness. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The published version drops the orbifold option. After noting that for general K one should regard [G]_K as an orbifold, it says 'but we will restrict our attention to the torsion-free case'. The item's 'in general [G]_K is treated as an orbifold' follows the preprint. Review note: Planned ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.0 fits the space itself. The Hecke action on (co)homology is ALS.3 (Hecke correspondences on complexes), which should be cited too. ALS.0 builds a centre correction into its X_K, while TV's [G]_K divides only by K_∞. When G has a split central torus the two differ by a free proper action of the contractible group A_G(R)^0, so their cohomology agrees; for G semisimple they coincide. The item should state which it uses.

items.name: The Hecke algebra is a restricted tensor product
items.statement: H(G(A_f),K) is the restricted tensor product over finite places of the H(G_v,K_v) with respect to their identity elements; for V a set of finite places H(G_V,K_V) denotes the restricted tensor product over V.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.1 (the paragraph after Definition 5.1; preprint p. 16); published version: §5.1, the paragraph after the Definition, p. 196
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups plans restricted products of locally compact groups and the adelic level maps; this is the Hecke-algebra form of that decomposition. Review note: Same text in both versions. The planned citation is loose. AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.0 plans restricted products of groups and Haar measures, and AA.4 plans level maps and Hecke correspondences. Neither states the restricted-tensor-product decomposition H(G(A_f),K) = ⊗'_v H(G_v,K_v) of the k-valued Hecke algebra. The nearest planned statement is AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.0 (test functions as restricted tensor products), with SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.1 for local Hecke algebras over rings. Either cite AF.0 and SR.1, or mark the item missing and route it to route 1.

items.name: Good places
items.statement: A finite place v is good for (G,K,p) if (i) the residue characteristic of O_v is not p, (ii) G×_F F_v is quasisplit over F_v and split over an unramified extension, and (iii) K_v is hyperspecial, i.e. of the form Ƥ(O_v) for a reductive smooth model Ƥ. All but finitely many places are good, and at a good place H(G_v,K_v) is a commutative integral domain whose characters are described by the Satake isomorphism.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.2 (preprint p. 16); published version: §5.2 (Good places), p. 196
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 plans parahoric and hyperspecial group schemes and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 the Satake isomorphism at a hyperspecial level; the almost-all statement is the standard spreading-out argument. Review note: The statement matches. Both versions misprint (iii) as 'a reductive smooth model for 𝔊 ×_F F_v' where G ×_F F_v is meant (new misprint issue); the item already has the intended reading. The planned citations are right in part. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 plans hyperspecial models. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 plans Satake at hyperspecial level, but it must supply k-coefficients with char k = p ≠ residue characteristic, and the integral-domain property. No layer plans the spreading-out statement that all but finitely many places are good; it should be added to route 1 or requested from SR.4. The published text points to §7.2 for Satake.

items.name: Characters persist under shrinking the level away from V (Proposition 5.4)
items.statement: Let K = ∏K_v and K' = ∏K'_v with K'_v ⊂ K_v for all v and K'_v = K_v for v ∈ V. If a character χ of H(G_V,K_V) appears in the cohomology of [G]_K then it appears in the cohomology of [G]_{K'}.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Proposition 5.4 (preprint p. 16); published version: Proposition 5.4, p. 197 (context: §5.3, p. 197)
items.note: Proved with the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^i(K/K';H^j([G]_{K'})) of H_V-modules and the bar model. It is what lets one assume the level is neat, so that [G]_K is a manifold. Review note: Same in both versions. The context, not repeated in the item, is: V a set of finite good places and χ a character of H(G_V,K_V), with 'appears' as defined in §5.3 (a proposed new item). The proof uses the Hochschild–Serre (Cartan–Leray) spectral sequence for the finite group K/K′ acting on [G]_{K′}, the bar model, and finite-dimensionality of the cohomology. Status missing is right.

items.name: The σ-action setup on a pair of locally symmetric spaces
items.statement: Let σ act on G with order p and H = G^σ connected. Fix a σ-stable level structure K for G with U = K^σ the level for H; fix K_∞ ⊂ G(F_∞) maximal compact, σ-invariant, meeting H(F_∞) in a maximal compact U_∞; write [G]_K and [H]_U for the two locally symmetric spaces; and assume K sufficiently small, so that G(F)∩K_∞K is trivial.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.5 (preprint p. 16); published version: §5.5 (σ-action), conditions (a)–(d), p. 197
items.note: The σ-invariant maximal compact is found inside G(F_∞)⋊⟨σ⟩. This setup is the standing hypothesis for the rest of the paper. Review note: Same content. The published text restates G as the connected reductive group of §2.3 and says 'We will always assume that H is connected'. Status missing is right.

items.name: Almost all places are σ-good (Proposition 5.6)
items.statement: Say a finite place v is σ-good for (G,K,H,U) if v is good for K and U and K_v ⊂ G_v is σ-plain. If H = G^σ is connected, then all but finitely many places of F are σ-good.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Proposition 5.6 (statement preprint p. 17, proof pp. 17–18); published version: Proposition 5.6, statement p. 197, proof p. 198
items.note: The proof spreads out the morphism g ↦ g^{-1}σ(g) over O_F, uses the closedness of the conjugacy class of the finite-order (hence semisimple) σ in characteristic zero to make its image closed away from a finite set T, and then applies Steinberg's theorem over the residue field together with the prime-to-p pro-order of the congruence kernel. Review note: The statement matches in both versions. The published proof adds an opening sentence that makes the reduction explicit. Two new issues concern the proof, and both are also in the preprint: the misprint (xg)^{−1}σ(gx) for (gx)^{−1}σ(gx), and an unstated enlargement of T needed to make the special fibre of the fixed-point scheme 𝔊^σ connected before Lang–Steinberg applies. The remark that Conrad and Prasad sharpened this via tori is in both versions. Status missing is right.

items.name: [H]_U is a union of components of the σ-fixed locus (Proposition, §5.7)
items.statement: With V a nonempty finite set of σ-good places and X = G(F)\G(A_F)/K^{(V)}, the natural map [H]_U → X^σ/K_V^σ is a homeomorphism onto a union of connected components of X^σ/K_V^σ.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.7, the unnumbered Proposition (preprint p. 18; proof pp. 18–19); published version: §5.7 (Analysis of connected components), the unnumbered Proposition, p. 199, proof pp. 199–200
items.note: Proved by constructing the locally constant invariant e: X^σ/K_V^σ → H^1(σ,G(F))×H^1(σ,K^{(V)}), showing the map is injective and that its image is the fibre over the trivial class, and then a properness argument from reduction theory. Review note: The statement matches. Equation numbers differ between the versions. In the published text X = G(F)\G(A_F)/K^(V) is (5.7.1) and the map e is (5.7.2); in the preprint X is unnumbered and e is (5.7.1). The published proof also adds a reference: Rohlfs–Speh, Math. Ann. 296 (1993), §0.4. In both versions the proof reuses U_∞ and U for a σ-stable neighbourhood of K_∞ and for U_∞·K, although §5.5 already defines them as K_∞ ∩ H(F_∞) and K^σ (new misprint issue). The map e and its local constancy are proposed as a separate new item. Status missing is right.

items.name: Properness of [H]_U → G(F)\G(A)
items.statement: The continuous injection [H]_U → X^σ/K_V^σ of §5.7 is proper onto its image, so it is a homeomorphism onto that image. This rests on properness of H(F)\H(A_F) → G(F)\G(A_F) for the connected reductive F-subgroup H = G^σ of G. Published proof: a statement of Borel–Prasad, cf. Ash (2003), Lemma 2.7, or as in Platonov–Rapinchuk, Lemma 4.15. Preprint outline: by reduction theory there is a compact Ω ⊂ H(A_F) with A^+·Ω → H(F)\H(A_F) surjective, A^+ the positive cone in the connected real points of a maximal F-split torus of H; this reduces to properness of A_G^+ → G(F)\G(A), which is again reduction theory.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.7; in the proof of the unnumbered Proposition (the parenthetical outline, preprint p. 19); published version: §5.7, last sentence of the proof of the Proposition, p. 200, where the outline is replaced by references
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.3 plans reduction theory, Siegel sets and the geometry of arithmetic quotients; the paper says it knows no reference for this properness statement, which uses the reductivity of H. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The published version removes the preprint's reduction-theory outline (the compact Ω with A^+·Ω surjective, and the reduction to properness of A_G^+ → G(F)\G(A)), together with the remark that no reference is known. It says instead: 'the properness is a statement of Borel–Prasad (cf. Lemma 2.7 of [1]); it can also be deduced as in Lemma 4.15 of [28]'. Here [1] is Ash, Smith theory and Hecke operators, J. Algebra 259 (2003), and [28] is Platonov–Rapinchuk, Algebraic Groups and Number Theory. The item's note 'the paper says it knows no reference' holds only for the preprint. Review note: The citation of AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.3 is only partly right. AA.3 plans Siegel sets and finiteness, but not the properness of H(F)\H(A) → G(F)\G(A) for a reductive subgroup. Keep AA.3 as a prerequisite and mark this properness statement missing (route 1), or ask for it to be added to AA.3.

items.name: First Main Theorem: mod p functoriality from H = G^σ to G (Theorem 5.8)
items.statement: Let G,H,U,K,σ be as in §5.5 and V a nonempty set of σ-good places. Then H(G_V,K_V) and H(H_V,U_V) are commutative integral domains, so nBr: H(G_V,K_V) → H(H_V,U_V) is defined; and if χ: H(H_V,U_V) → k is an eigenvalue occurring in the cohomology of [H]_U, then χ ∘ nBr occurs in the cohomology of [G]_K. Equivalently: if a mod p automorphic form for G^σ has Satake parameters {a_v}, there is a mod p automorphic form for G with Satake parameters {ψ_v^*(a_v)}.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Theorem 5.8 (preprint p. 19), stated in §1.1 as the 'First Main Theorem'; published version: Theorem 5.8, p. 200, stated in §1.1 (p. 177) as the 'Main Theorem' (the word 'First' is dropped with the Second Main Theorem)
items.note: No lift to characteristic zero is assumed for either eigenclass. The reduction to finite V uses the finite-dimensionality of the cohomology; the rest is Theorem 4.4 applied through §5.7. Review note: The statement matches the published text. The published proof ends with 'Now apply Theorem 4.4.' and no longer mentions Theorem 7.2 for checking the hypotheses; the integral-domain property is still referred to Theorem 7.2. The 'equivalently' clause is the introduction's Satake-parameter reformulation. It needs §7, and Theorem 8.10 to identify ψ_v^*; it is a translation, not a separate result. The proof depends on Theorem 4.4, so it inherits the convergence gap in step (3) of that proof (new issue). The (a) ⇒ (b) finiteness gap does not affect it, because H^*([G]_K) is finite-dimensional. Status missing is right.

items.name: Admissible k-representations of G_v and σ-fixed representations
items.statement: Fix a finite place v of F of residue characteristic ≠ p. A k-representation Π of G_v is smooth (every vector has open stabiliser) and admissible (Π^{K′} is finite-dimensional over k for every compact open subgroup K′ ⊂ G_v). Such a Π is σ-fixed if Π ≅ Π∘σ.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.1 (preprint p. 19); published version: §6.1 (Linkage and the Brauer homomorphism), first two paragraphs, p. 201
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0 plans the smooth abelian category over arbitrary coefficients, invariants under compact opens and admissibility; SR.1 explicitly excludes characteristic p from the Hecke-module equivalence and prescribes working in the smooth action category there, which is the setting TV16 uses. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item drops the standing hypothesis of §6.1: the finite place v has residue characteristic ≠ p (and K_v need not be maximal compact). Both versions also write 'K′ ⊂ G' for a compact open subgroup of G_v. Review note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0 fits. It plans smoothness and admissibility; its admissibility, finite generation of invariants, is finite-dimensionality over the field k. The σ-fixed condition is not planned anywhere but is a one-line definition.

items.name: A σ-fixed irreducible admissible representation has a unique compatible σ-action
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of residue characteristic ≠ p and Π an irreducible admissible σ-fixed k-representation of G_v. Then there is a unique action of σ on Π (a k-linear automorphism of order dividing p) compatible with the σ-action on G_v.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.1, the unnumbered Proposition (preprint p. 19); published version: §6.1, the unnumbered Proposition, p. 201
items.note: An intertwiner A between Π and Π∘σ has A^p scalar by Schur's lemma applied to Π^{K_v^0} for a prime-to-p open K_v^0; rescaling by the p-th root of that scalar gives the action, and the p-th root is unique in k. Review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits that v has residue characteristic ≠ p. The proof needs this to choose an open subgroup K_v^0 of prime-to-p pro-order. Review note: Both versions misprint the proof: Π^{K_v^0} is called an irreducible representation of H(G_v, K_v) where H(G_v, K_v^0) is meant (new misprint issue). The printed proof shows only existence. Uniqueness follows because two compatible actions differ by a G_v-automorphism, which is a scalar c by Schur's lemma, and c^p = 1 forces c = 1 in characteristic p. The published text adds a comparison with Glauberman [17, Th. 1]. Status missing is right.

items.name: Linkage of local representations
items.statement: An irreducible representation π of H_v is linked with a σ-fixed irreducible Π of G_v if the Frobenius twist π^{(p)} occurs as a Jordan–Hoelder constituent of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Definition 6.2 (preprint p. 20); published version: Definition 6.2, p. 201
items.note: Motivating example: G = H^p with σ cyclic permutation, where π_v is linked with π_v^{⊗p}. This is the representation-theoretic shadow of the Brauer homomorphism. Review note: Same in both versions. The motivating example after the definition (π_v is linked with π_v^{⊗p} for G = H^p) is proposed as a new item under coverage. Status missing is right.

items.name: Linkage is compatible with the Brauer homomorphism
items.statement: Let K_v be σ-plain, so H_v/U_v = (G_v/K_v)^σ. Then for every h ∈ H(G_v,K_v)^σ the square formed by T^*(Π^{K_v}) → T^*(Π)^{U_v} and the actions of T^*(h) and Br(h) commutes.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.1; the displayed diagram (6.1) [wrong: the diagram is labelled (6.2.1) in both versions and follows Definition 6.2, so it lies in §6.2 of the printed numbering; preprint p. 20]; published version: §6.2, diagram (6.2.1) and its proof, p. 202
items.note: The computation reduces to the fact that σ acts freely on (G_v/K_v) − H_v/U_v, so the difference of the two sums lies in NΠ. Review note: The statement is correct. The proof uses only condition (a) of σ-plainness, H_v/U_v = (G_v/K_v)^σ, and Π need not be irreducible, only σ-fixed with its σ-action. §4.2 of the published text refers to (6.2.1) as the more general statement, and §8.15 uses it to compute the unramified Brauer homomorphism. Status missing is right.

items.name: Conjecture: Tate cohomology of an admissible representation has finite length
items.statement: Conjecture: if Π is a σ-fixed irreducible admissible representation of G_v then T^*Π has finite length as an H_v-representation.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.3, the first conjecture (preprint p. 21); published version: §6.3 (Conjectures), the first displayed conjecture, p. 202
items.note: Motivated by the analogy with the Jacquet functor, which carries admissibles to admissibles. Recorded as a conjecture, not a theorem. Review note: Same in both versions. Status missing is right; it is a conjecture and is recorded as one.

items.name: Conjecture: linkage realises functoriality for a σ-dual homomorphism
items.statement: Conjecture: linkage is compatible with the Langlands functorial transfer attached to a σ-dual homomorphism ^Lψ: ^LH → ^LG; in particular if a σ-fixed Π of G_v is linked with π of H_v then ^Lψ should carry the Langlands parameter of π to that of Π.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.3, the second conjecture (preprint p. 21); published version: §6.3, the second displayed conjecture and the paragraph after it, pp. 202–203
items.note: Left deliberately imprecise in the paper; the supporting evidence is depth-zero base change for GL_n, and work of Ronchetti in the supercuspidal case. Review note: Same content. The published text cites Definition 9.1 for the σ-dual homomorphism ^Lψ: ^LĤ → ^LĜ. The preprint cites §1.2 and §7.7. The evidence is the authors' depth-zero base-change computations for GL_n; Ronchetti's supercuspidal evidence is mentioned in published §1.5(i), p. 182.

items.name: The G_S-module π(χ) attached to a Hecke character
items.statement: For V a finite set of good places, S a finite set of finite places disjoint from V, and χ: H(G_V,K_V) → k a character, π(χ) is the localisation at the maximal ideal of χ of the direct limit over level structures K' agreeing with K away from S of H^*([G]_{K'}); it and all its irreducible subquotients are admissible.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.4 (preprint p. 21); published version: §6.4 (Ramified places), including (6.4.1), p. 203
items.note: Its precise determination is the subject of the mod p Langlands correspondence. Admissibility comes from shrinking K' so that K'_S has prime-to-p pro-order and [G]_{K'} is a manifold with finite-dimensional cohomology. Review note: The statement matches. In both versions §6.4 lets S be any finite set of finite places disjoint from V. The admissibility argument (shrink K′ until K′_S has prime-to-p pro-order) is available only when S contains no place above p (new gap issue, affects nothing). Theorem 6.5, the only use, assumes this. The item should either add 'S disjoint from the places above p' or cite a separate admissibility argument at p-adic places. Status missing is right.

items.name: Functoriality at ramified places (Theorem 6.5)
items.statement: Let G,H,K,U,σ be as in §5.5 with G semisimple and H connected, V a finite set of σ-good places and S a finite set of finite places disjoint from V and from the primes above p. Let χ: H(H_V,U_V) → k and ψ = χ ∘ nBr. Then every irreducible subquotient of the H_S-module π(χ) is linked with an irreducible subquotient of the G_S-module Π(ψ).
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), Theorem 6.5 (preprint p. 21; proof p. 21); published version: Theorem 6.5, p. 203, with the remark and proof on p. 204
items.note: Proved as Theorem 5.8 but in cohomology and at all levels simultaneously, then localising; the passage from χ∘Br to χ∘nBr is again the Frobenius argument on coefficients. The restriction that V be finite is expected to be removable. Review note: The statement matches. The proof needs three caveats. (1) It relies on the Smith double complex of the direct limit of cochain complexes, 'convergent because the cohomological dimension of [G]_{K′} is bounded', so it inherits the convergence gap of Theorem 4.4. (2) It writes H(H_V, K_V) for H(H_V, U_V) twice (new misprint issue). (3) It stops at 'τ^{(p)} is a composition factor of T^*Π(ψ)'. The remaining step to linkage with an irreducible σ-fixed subquotient of Π(ψ) is not written. It is routine: T^* commutes with filtered colimits; finitely generated admissible G_S-representations with ℓ ≠ p have finite length (Vignéras); and σ-orbits of p non-isomorphic constituents have T^* = 0. Status missing is right.

items.name: The restricted Weyl group at a place
items.statement: For v a good place, A_v ⊂ B_v a maximally split torus and Borel of G_v, W_{0,v} = N_{G_v}(A_v)/Cent_{G_v}(A_v); it acts compatibly on unramified characters of T_v and on splittings of T-hat(k)⋊Frob_v → ⟨Frob_v⟩, and on the dual torus A-hat_v.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §7.1; published version: §7.1 (Restricted Weyl group), pp. 204–205
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1 plans relative roots, the relative Weyl group and valued root data for nonsplit groups over local fields, and layer 7 of the Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap plans the relative root system for nonsplit groups. Review note: Same content in print (the published text writes Z_{G_v}(A_v) for the centraliser). Planned status is reasonable: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1 plans the relative Weyl group, and Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 7 the relative root system; the compatibility with unramified characters of T_v and with splittings of LT̂_v is the §2.9 torus correspondence and is not planned there.

items.name: The restricted Weyl action is induced by Frobenius-fixed elements of the dual group
items.statement: The action of any w ∈ W_{0,v} on A-hat_v is induced by an element n ∈ G-hat(k) normalising T-hat and fixed by Frob_v.
items.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §7.1, the unnumbered Proposition; published version: §7.1, unnumbered Proposition, p. 205 (proof pp. 205–206)
items.note: Needed to compare the Satake isomorphism on the dual torus with invariant functions on the twisted dual group. Review note: Statement unchanged in print. The published proof is fuller: it reduces to the simply connected almost simple case with Frob_v transitive on simple roots, where only SL_2 (trivial action) and SL_3 (g ↦ ω(g^t)^{-1}ω, with the Frob-fixed representative ω = antidiag(1,−1,1)) occur.

items.name: The twisted action of the restricted Weyl group on the dual torus
