items.locator: published version: §1.2.4 (Exceptional groups), pp. 179–180, including (1.2.1); precise form §9.7, pp. 223–226, including (9.7.1) and the Proposition there; preprint arXiv:1407.2346v1: §1.2 (p. 2, the order-3 inner automorphism of G_2) and Proposition 10.6 (item 94)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): This is the paper's showcase exceptional example. The embedding exists only in characteristic 3. The preprint treats the inner order-3 automorphism of G_2 inside its case analysis (Proposition 10.6, item 94, and the discussion on its p. 2). If the §9 checker proposes an item for the Proposition of §9.7 (ψ_1 extends to Ĥ ↪ Ĝ, and ψ_1∘Frob extends the dual norm), this item should cite it. Route: SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP.

items.name: The mod p cyclotomic character
items.statement: cyclo: Γ_F → F_p^× ⊂ k^× is the character through which Γ_F = Gal(F̄/F) acts on the group μ_p(F̄) of p-th roots of unity: γ(ζ) = ζ^{cyclo(γ)} for all ζ ∈ μ_p(F̄).
items.locator: published version: §2.1 (Notation used throughout), p. 184; preprint arXiv:1407.2346v1, §2.1
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): This is a definition the paper uses: in the canonical pseudoroots (published §9.3(b), (9.3.1)), in the choice of ϖ_γ in §9.7, and in the preprint's §7.5. No item covers it. Mathlib has it. The text's 'pth roots of unity in F' is a misprint for F̄: see issues.

items.name: Smith theory for Hecke modules, Tate-cohomology form
items.statement: Let G be a locally compact totally disconnected group, K ⊂ G a compact open subgroup, and X a locally compact Hausdorff right G-space on which K acts freely and properly. Let σ of order p act compatibly on G, K and X, with G^σ, K^σ, X^σ again satisfying these conditions. Assume X/K has finite cohomological dimension and K is σ-plain. Make H_*(X^σ/K^σ) an H(G,K)^σ-module through Br. Then for every j, H_j(X^σ/K^σ) is isomorphic as an H(G,K)^σ-module to a subquotient of T^*H_*(X/K) = ⊕_{i∈{0,1}, m≥0} T^i H_m(X/K). Dually, each H^j(X^σ/K^σ) is a subquotient of T^*H^*(X/K). The proof compares the two spectral sequences of the Smith double complex, and it needs a bounded chain model with compatible σ- and Hecke actions; see the new issue on step (3).
items.locator: published version: §4.4, end of the proof of Theorem 4.4 (step (3), after (4.4.4)), p. 196; arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), same place (§4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4, step (3)), p. 15
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): The proof proves more than Theorem 4.4(a): H_*(X^σ/K^σ) is an H(G,K)^σ-subquotient of T^*H_*(X/K). The proof of Theorem 6.5 uses this form ('an embedding of H^*([H]_{U′}) as a subquotient of T^*H^*([G]_{K′})'), and so does §8. No item states it: item 31 has only the composition-factor form, and item 33 only the E^2 page. Route: SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality.

items.name: A Hecke character appears in the cohomology of [G]_K
items.statement: Let V be a set of finite places that are good for (G, K, p) (§5.2), and χ: H(G_V,K_V) → k a k-algebra homomorphism. χ appears in the cohomology of [G]_K if some nonzero h ∈ H^*([G]_K) (k-coefficients, K ∩ G(F) torsion-free) satisfies t·h = χ(t)h for all t ∈ H(G_V,K_V).
items.locator: published version: §5.3 (Characters of the Hecke algebra appearing in cohomology), p. 197; arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.3, p. 16
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): Items 39 and 44 and Theorem 6.5 all use this definition, but no item states it. Route: SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality.

items.name: The Rohlfs–Speh invariant of σ-fixed points of G(F)\G(A_F)/K^(V)
items.statement: Let G, H = G^σ, K, U and K_∞ be as in §5.5; in particular G(F) ∩ K_∞K = 1. Let V be a nonempty finite set of σ-good places, K^(V) = K_∞∏_{w∉V}K_w and X = G(F)\G(A_F)/K^(V), on which K_V = ∏_{w∈V}K_w acts freely. (i) For g ∈ G(A_F), the point G(F)gK^(V) is σ-fixed iff σ(g) = γgκ for some γ ∈ G(F) and κ ∈ K^(V). Then γ = σ(g_w)g_w^{−1} for each w ∈ V, so γ and κ are unique. The maps σ ↦ γ^{−1} and σ ↦ κ are 1-cocycles, and their classes depend only on the image of g in X^σ/K_V^σ. This defines e: X^σ/K_V^σ → H^1(σ, G(F)) × H^1(σ, K^(V)). (ii) e is locally constant; the proof uses proper discontinuity and freeness of the G(F)-action, and that H^1(σ, K_∞) is finite with the discrete topology. (iii) The fibre of e over the trivial class is the image of the natural map [H]_U → X^σ/K_V^σ, which is injective.
items.locator: published version: §5.7, (5.7.2) and the proof of the unnumbered Proposition, pp. 199–200 (citing Rohlfs–Speh, Math. Ann. 296 (1993), §0.4); arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §5.7, (5.7.1) and the proof of the unnumbered Proposition, pp. 18–19
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): The proof of the §5.7 Proposition, the step that identifies [H]_U with a union of components of X^σ/K_V^σ, rests on this construction and lemma: the nonabelian-cohomology invariant e, its local constancy, and the description of its trivial fibre. Item 42 mentions it only in its note. Route: SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality.

items.name: Linkage for the cyclic permutation action on H^p
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of residue characteristic ≠ p, H_v the F_v-points of a connected reductive group, and G_v = H_v^p with σ cyclically permuting the factors, so G_v^σ = H_v diagonally. Let π be an irreducible admissible k-representation of H_v. Then Π = π^{⊗p}, with σ permuting the tensor factors, is an irreducible admissible σ-fixed representation of G_v. The map v ↦ v⊗⋯⊗v induces H_v-equivariant isomorphisms π^{(p)} ≅ T^0(π^{⊗p}) and π^{(p)} ≅ T^1(π^{⊗p}): it is additive modulo im N ⊂ im(1−σ), since N = (1−σ)^{p−1} in characteristic p, and it is Frobenius-semilinear. In particular π is linked with π^{⊗p} in the sense of Definition 6.2.
items.locator: published version: §6.2, the paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 201; arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §6.2, the paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 20
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): It is the basic example of linkage and explains the Frobenius twist. It is a checkable statement (a Tate-cohomology computation for tensor induction), and no item covers it; item 47 mentions it only in a note. Route: SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality.

items.name: Injectivity in Satake (ii): restriction to T̂⋊Frob_v and dominance of the conjugation map
items.statement: Let Ĝ carry its pinned action of Frob_v, with T̂ ⊂ B̂ Frob_v-stable, and let Â_v = T̂_{Frob_v}. (1) Every Ĝ-invariant regular function on Ĝ⋊Frob_v, restricted to T̂⋊Frob_v, descends to a regular function on Â_v, because tFrob_v and t·t'^{Frob_v}t'^{-1}Frob_v are conjugate by t'. This function is W_{0,v}-invariant for the usual action, by the Proposition of §7.1. (2) The conjugation map α: Ĝ×(T̂⋊Frob_v) → Ĝ⋊Frob_v, (g,x) ↦ gxg^{-1}, is dominant. The setwise stabiliser M of T̂⋊Frob_v in Ĝ has identity component T̂, and for generic t the fibre of α through (1,tFrob_v) has dimension dim T̂, so the image has dimension dim Ĝ. Hence a Ĝ-invariant regular function on Ĝ⋊Frob_v that vanishes on T̂⋊Frob_v is zero. Together with the Lemma of §7.3, restriction is therefore an isomorphism k[Ĝ⋊Frob_v]^Ĝ ≅ k[Â_v]^{W_{0,v}}.
items.locator: published version: §7.3, 'Proof of part (ii)', pp. 208–209; arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §7.3, 'Proof of part (ii)'
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): This is the injectivity half of Satake (ii) and a separate argument from the Lemma of §7.3. The extraction folds it wrongly into item 57's note. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Mod 2 Eisenstein series: the Frobenius-twisted block inclusion GL_a×GL_b → GL_n is σ-dual
items.statement: Let F be a number field, a,b ≥ 1, n = a+b, G = GL_n over F and σ = Ad(diag(1,…,1,−1,…,−1)) (a entries 1, b entries −1), an inner involution with H = G^σ = GL_a×GL_b. Let p = 2 and k be algebraically closed of characteristic 2, so that ^LH = (GL_a×GL_b)(k)×Γ_F and ^LG = GL_n(k)×Γ_F, with the canonical (trivial) pseudoroots, and let ι: GL_a×GL_b → GL_n be the block-diagonal inclusion. Take T_H = T_G the diagonal tori and B_H ⊂ B_G the upper-triangular Borels. Then (T_H,B_H,T_G,B_G) is Γ-admissible, the norm T_G → T_H is t ↦ t^2, and the dual norm is Frob∘ι on the diagonal tori. Hence ^Lψ(g,γ) = (Frob(ι(g)),γ) is a σ-dual homomorphism with respect to the canonical pseudoroots. Consequence (twisting by Frob^{-1} and iterating over GL_{n_1}×…×GL_{n_r} ⊂ GL_N, N = n_1+…+n_r): a mod 2 Hecke eigenclass in the cohomology of the locally symmetric space of GL_{n_1}×…×GL_{n_r} gives a mod 2 Hecke eigenclass for GL_N whose Satake parameters at almost all good places are the images of the original ones under the direct-sum inclusion of dual groups.
items.locator: Published version (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016)): §9.5 'Mod 2 Eisenstein series', pp. 222–223, with §1.2.3, p. 179 (where the index d in GL_{n_d} is a slip for r); not in arXiv:1407.2346v1
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): Published-only. The preprint's Second Main Theorem needs G simply connected and H semisimple, so GL_n ⊃ GL_a×GL_b is not treated there. This is a main example of the published paper. Route: SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP.

items.name: Exotic transfer from Sp_2n to SL_2n in characteristic 2
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2, G the split SL_{2n} over F, J ∈ SL_{2n}(Z) the standard antidiagonal skew-symmetric matrix and σ(g) = J(g^T)^{-1}J^{-1}, an involution with H = G^σ ≅ Sp_{2n} (for n = 1, σ is trivial). Let p = 2 and k be algebraically closed of characteristic 2, with ^LH = SO_{2n+1}(k)×Γ_F and ^LG = PGL_{2n}(k)×Γ_F. Here SO_{2n+1} is the group of determinant-one isometries of x_{2n+1}^2 + Σ_{i=1}^n x_i x_{2n+1−i}, pinned by diagonal and upper-triangular matrices. As an SO_{2n+1}-module, k^{2n+1} is an extension of a 2n-dimensional representation by the trivial line k·x_{2n+1}; let ι: SO_{2n+1} → PGL_{2n} be the projectivisation of that 2n-dimensional quotient. Take T_H ⊂ B_H and T_G ⊂ B_G the diagonal tori and upper-triangular Borels. Then (T_H,B_H,T_G,B_G) is Γ-admissible, the norm T_G → T_H is (t_1,…,t_{2n}) ↦ (t_1t_{2n}^{-1}, t_2t_{2n−1}^{-1}, …, t_{2n}t_1^{-1}), and the dual norm N̂ equals ι on T̂_H. Hence ^Lψ(h,γ) = (ι(h),γ) is a σ-dual homomorphism with respect to the canonical (trivial) pseudoroots. Consequence: a cohomological Hecke eigenform α for Sp_{2n} over F (for instance one of characteristic zero, reduced mod 2) gives a Hecke eigenclass e_α in the mod 2 cohomology of SL_{2n} whose Satake parameters are the images of those of α under ι, the 2n-dimensional representation SO_{2n+1} → GL_{2n} in characteristic 2.
items.locator: Published version: §9.6 'Exotic transfer from Sp_2n', p. 223, with §1.2.2, p. 179 (the printed norm formula (t_1t_{2n}, …, t_{2n}t_1) is a misprint, corrected here); preprint arXiv:1407.2346v1: the case (SL(2n),Sp(2n)), n ≥ 2, of Proposition 11.5 with Lemma 11.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): Published-only explicit example. In the preprint it is only the case (SL(2n),Sp(2n)) of Proposition 11.5 (item 99), with the dual norm extended abstractly by Lemma 11.4. Print identifies the σ-dual homomorphism as the 2n-dimensional representation of SO_{2n+1} in characteristic 2, which has no characteristic-zero lift. Route: SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP.

items.name: The short-root PGL_3 in G_2 in characteristic 3 extends ψ_1 (Proposition of §9.7)
items.statement: Let G be a form of G_2 over F and σ an F-automorphism of order 3 with H = G^σ a form of SL_3 (p = 3, char k = 3). Over F̄, σ = Ad(s) with s generating Z(H). Let T be an F-rational maximal torus of H, hence of G, and B_H ⊃ T a Borel of H with simple roots β_1, β_2 (long roots of G). Let α be the short root of T on G orthogonal to (β_1+β_2)^∨ that makes an obtuse angle with β_1, and B_G ⊃ B_H the Borel with simple roots {α, β_1}, so that β_2 = β_1+3α. The triple B_H ⊃ T ⊂ B_G gives ψ_1: T̂_H ≅ T̂_G with β_{1,*} ↦ β_{1,*} and β_{2,*} ↦ β_{1,*}+3α_*. Then (1) ψ_1 extends to an injective homomorphism ψ'_1: Ĥ ≅ PGL_3 → Ĝ = G_2 whose image Ĥ_1 is generated by T̂_G and the root groups of the six short roots of Ĝ; this is a subgroup because char k = 3. (2) ψ'_1∘Frob extends the dual norm T̂_H → T̂_G, since σ acts trivially on T and the norm is multiplication by 3 on X_*(T).
items.locator: Published version: §9.7 'Transfer from SL_3 to G_2', Proposition, p. 224 (proof p. 225, footnote 7); preprint arXiv:1407.2346v1: Proposition 10.1 and the proof of Proposition 10.3, case g_2 ⊃ sl_3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): This is the only printed instance of Propositions 10.1 and 10.3. It is the G_2 case with an explicit construction: Ĥ_1 is generated by the short root groups in characteristic 3. Items 89 and 91 are stated in general for the preprint. Route: SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP.

items.name: Transfer from SL_3 (or SU_3) to G_2 mod 3 is σ-dual
items.statement: In the situation of the preceding Proposition, let o be the outer automorphism of H fixing B_H and swapping β_1, β_2, and let w(o) = s_α ∈ W_G, the unique element exchanging the two Borels of G containing B_H, whose simple roots are {α,β_1} and {−α,β_2}. Both Borels are Γ-admissible with respect to (T,B_H). The Levi L̂_o ⊂ Ĝ with roots ±α^∨_* is isomorphic to GL_2. Let ι: SL_2 → Ĝ be the coroot homomorphism of α_*, J = (0 1; −1 0), t_0 ∈ Z(L̂_o) such that ι(J)t_0 has order 2, and ẇ(o) = ι(J)t_0. Fix a pinning of Ĥ_1 preserved by ẇ(o) and let ψ'_1 be the pinned extension. For γ ∈ Γ_F put ϖ_γ = 1 if γ acts trivially on the root datum of H and ϖ_γ = ẇ(o) otherwise; γ acts nontrivially exactly when cyclo(γ) ≡ −1 mod 3. Then ^Lψ(h⋊γ) = ψ'_1(Frob(h))ϖ_γ⋊γ is a homomorphism ^LH → ^LG and a σ-dual homomorphism with respect to the canonical pseudoroots; at γ with cyclo(γ) = −1 one has ρ^-_H(γ) = α_*(−1)⋊γ and ρ^-_G(γ) = α_*(−1)β_{1,*}(−1)⋊γ, and ẇ(o) and β_{1,*}(−1) are non-central involutions of L̂_o ≅ GL_2, hence conjugate. Consequence (§1.2.4): for U_3 the unitary group of F(√−3)/F (GL_3 if √−3 ∈ F), mod 3 Hecke eigenclasses on SU_3 lift to mod 3 Hecke eigenclasses on a form of G_2, with Satake parameters related by ι: PGL_3 ⋊ ⟨w⟩ ↪ G_2 (PGL_3 on the short roots, w the pinned outer automorphism). This embedding exists only in characteristic 3.
items.locator: Published version: §9.7, pp. 223–226, (9.7.1) and (9.7.2) on p. 225, verification p. 226, with §1.2.4, pp. 179–180 (printed (9.7.1) has ψ_1 for ψ'_1; the cyclotomic equivalence is asserted without proof in print and proved in preprint Proposition 10.6 Step 1); preprint arXiv:1407.2346v1: Proposition 10.6, case g_2 ⊃ sl_3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 (coverage of the paper): This is the printed version of Proposition 10.6 in the g_2 case, with its own construction of ẇ(o) and its own verification (9.7.2). §1.3 names it as the model for the inner cases. Route: SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP.

routes.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality
routes.brief:
Plan Smith theory for the cohomology of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and the mod p functoriality it produces. The final theorems are the paper's Theorem 4.4 and Theorem 5.8 and its Theorem 6.5. Theorem 4.4: let G be locally compact totally disconnected, K a compact open subgroup, X a locally compact Hausdorff space with a free proper right K-action and a continuous right G-action, and let sigma of order p act compatibly on G, K and X, with X/K of finite cohomological dimension and K sigma-plain; then, regarding H^*(X/K) and H^*(X^sigma/K^sigma) as modules over H(G,K)^sigma by restriction and through the Brauer homomorphism, every composition factor of the second is a composition factor of the first, and, when both Hecke algebras are commutative integral domains, every Hecke eigenvalue chi of the second gives the eigenvalue chi o nBr of the first. Theorem 5.8 (the First Main Theorem): for G semisimple over a number field F with sigma of order p and H = G^sigma connected, sigma-stable level K with U = K^sigma, and V a nonempty set of sigma-good places, H(G_V,K_V) and H(H_V,U_V) are commutative integral domains and every Hecke eigensystem chi occurring in H^*([H]_U ; k) gives the eigensystem chi o nBr occurring in H^*([G]_K ; k), with no assumption that either class lifts to characteristic zero. Theorem 6.5: with the same data, V finite and S a finite set of finite places disjoint from V and from the places above p, every irreducible subquotient of the H_S-module pi(chi) is linked with an irreducible subquotient of the G_S-module Pi(chi o nBr), where linkage means that the Frobenius twist occurs in the Tate cohomology. Cover: Tate cohomology of an order p action on the compactly supported sections of an equivariant sheaf on an l-space, and on a commutative k-algebra, with the bijection Hom(A,k)^sigma = Hom(T^0 A,k) that makes characters extend uniquely; sigma-plain compact open subgroups and the nonabelian cohomology they are defined by; the Brauer homomorphism of Hecke algebras and its normalization nBr; the Smith double complex, the degeneration of one of its spectral sequences and the convergence of the other; the sigma-action set-up on a pair of locally symmetric spaces, sigma-good places and the fact that almost all places are sigma-good; the identification of [H]_U with a union of connected components of the sigma-fixed locus; linkage of local representations, the conjectures of section 6.3, and the behaviour at ramified places; and the definition of a sigma-dual homomorphism together with the restatement of Theorem 5.8 as a functorial lift of modular Galois representations. Import from: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) for the spaces, their local systems and chain complexes and the Hecke correspondences on them; Adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients (AdelicAlgebraicGroups) for adelic points, level maps and reduction theory; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the smooth category over k, admissibility, Hecke algebras over rings and the Satake isomorphism; and Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: prime-order automorphisms, dual norms and sigma-dual homomorphisms in characteristic p (SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP) for the computation of nBr on Satake parameters and for the existence of sigma-dual homomorphisms. Tate cohomology of a finite group is already in the libraries and must not be rebuilt.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16), made against the published version (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 177–228), which numbers §§2–6 as the preprint does:
- Define nBr through the norm product: br(h) is the coefficientwise p-th root of Br(h ∗ h^σ ∗ ⋯ ∗ h^{σ^{p−1}}). The displayed (4.3.1), with the p-fold self-convolution, is wrong when h is not σ-invariant (GL_1 × GL_1 counterexample). It is not used later.
- Theorem 4.4: run the Smith double-complex comparison on a bounded complex, such as cellular chains of a σ-stable, K-equivariant triangulation, or use sheaf-theoretic Smith theory. With unbounded singular chains, step (3)'s convergence claim does not follow from vanishing of H_*(X/K) in high degrees. The same applies to the proof of Theorem 6.5. Part (b) needs H^*(X/K) finite-dimensional, which holds for [G]_K.
- Proposition 5.6: also exclude the finitely many places where the special fibre of the fixed-point scheme 𝔊^σ is disconnected, where σ does not extend, or where K_v ≠ 𝔊(O_v). Lang's theorem needs a connected special fibre.
- §2.11: C_m(X/K) is the K-coinvariants k[Hom(Δ^m, X)/K], not the K-invariants, which vanish.
- §6.4: the admissibility argument needs S to contain no place above p.
routes.reason: The parent roadmap owns exactly the objects this part of the paper acts on: the symmetric space and its arithmetic quotients (ALS.0), local systems and chain complexes at finite level (ALS.1), and Hecke correspondences on those complexes with their coherence data in the derived category (ALS.3). What the paper adds is a Z/p-action on that whole package and the fixed-point localisation it supports: Tate cohomology of the action on sheaves over l-spaces and on Hecke algebras, the Brauer homomorphism and its normalization, the Smith double complex, and the identification of [H]_U with a union of components of the sigma-fixed locus. None of that is planned anywhere in the atlas: a search for Smith theory returns nothing, and the only Tate cohomology in the atlas is the class-formation layer of the Tau Ceti class field theory roadmap. It is new layers in the direction of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces rather than a new roadmap, because every statement is about the cohomology of the spaces that roadmap builds and about the Hecke action it constructs. It is deliberately disjoint from the other Part II proposed for the same parent, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpacesPartII (the derived Hecke algebra and the reciprocity law, from PAPER-VENKATESH-19), which plans a derived enhancement of the Hecke action in characteristic zero and says nothing about group actions on the spaces.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: prime-order automorphisms, dual norms and σ-dual homomorphisms in characteristic p
routes.brief:
Plan the structure theory in characteristic p that computes the Brauer homomorphism on Satake parameters and constructs sigma-dual homomorphisms of L-groups. The final theorems are the paper's Theorem of section 8.1 and its Theorem 9.1. Theorem of section 8.1: let H = G^sigma be connected with sigma of prime order p, let v be a sigma-good place with Frobenius element gamma, fix local pseudoroots for G and H, let N-hat : T-hat_H to T-hat_G be the dual norm attached to a gamma-admissible Borel class and L-hat_gamma the associated dual Levi; then for every k-point x of (H-hat semidirect gamma) quotient H-hat there is t in T-hat_H(k) such that t rho_H^{-1}(gamma) represents x and N-hat(t) rho_G^{-1}(gamma) represents the image of x under Spec(nBr), and t may be chosen so that N-hat(t) lies in the centre of L-hat_gamma. Theorem 9.1 (the Second Main Theorem): if G is simply connected, sigma is an F-rational automorphism of prime order and H = G^sigma is semisimple, and (Lie G, Lie H) contains no factor isomorphic to (e_6, sl_3^3 or sl_6 x sl_2 or sp_8), then a sigma-dual homomorphism ^Lpsi : ^LH to ^LG exists with respect to the canonical pseudoroots. Cover: the canonical torus of a reductive group and global and canonical pseudoroots; Borel-de Siebenthal subgroups for an inner automorphism of order p and the dual endoscopic subgroups of G-hat, with the quasi-closed sets of roots that classify them; the C-group and the c-group and the PGL_2 counterexample showing that no sigma-dual homomorphism of L-groups or of C-groups need exist; the centraliser theory of section 8, namely that the centraliser of a maximal torus of H is a maximal torus of G, the split part of a gamma-fixed torus, the Levi L_G(gamma) and its derived group, gamma-admissible Borels with their existence lemma, the norm and dual norm homomorphisms, the rationality statements and the extension of unramified characters to the parabolic; the criterion of section 8.15 for recognising a sigma-dual homomorphism and Lemma 8.16; and the whole construction of sections 9 to 12: cyclic base change, the passage to the simply connected cover, the reduction to the absolutely almost simple case, the classification tables, Borel triples and the extension of psi_1 to the dual groups, the inner case with the element U for p = 3, the criteria for inner involutions and for pinned automorphisms with the exceptional isogenies they use, and the remaining computations including the embedding of Sp(2n) into the pinned fixed points of SO(2n+2) in characteristic 2 and the order 5 inner automorphism of E_8 with fixed points sl_5 x sl_5. Import from: Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) for algebraic groups, tori, Borel and parabolic subgroups, root data with their Galois action, pinned Chevalley-Demazure group schemes, the Frobenius on points and the special isogenies in characteristics 2 and 3, which are existing work and must not be re-planned; Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for relative roots, hyperspecial parahorics and the integral dual group and L-group; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the Satake isomorphism and unramified parabolic induction; and Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality (SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality) for the Brauer homomorphism, its normalization and the definition of a sigma-dual homomorphism.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16):
- The published version keeps §§7.1–7.4 and §§8.3–8.9 with their numbers. The Theorem of the preprint's §8.1 is the published Theorem 8.10, proved in §8.15. The preprint's §§2.12–2.13, §7.8, Theorem 7.9, the §8.15 criterion, Lemma 8.16 and §§9–12 are not in print.
- Theorem 9.1 (the Second Main Theorem) is only announced in print (§1.3, p. 181: 'Details will appear elsewhere'). The preprint gives no proof of its Theorem 12.1(i)–(iii) (the so_8 ⊃ sl_3, sl_2n ⊃ so_2n, so_2n+2 ⊃ so_2a+1 × so_2b+1 and so_2n ⊃ so_2a × so_2b rows). The Part II must prove these cases, or state its final theorem without them. State (ii)–(iii) for Spin forms, since for the SO forms G^σ is disconnected.
- The Satake normalisations are inverted. In (7.2.1), §7.4(a)(i) and (7.4.3), replace q_v by q_v^{-1}, so that the twist is w ∗ a = wa·√(wΣ*_G/Σ*_G)(q_v) and a pseudoroot satisfies α0² = Σ*_G(q_v)^{-1}. Then (7.2.6), §7.4(b), (7.5.3) and Theorem 8.10 hold together, as a PGL_2 check confirms.
- Remark 9.2's canonical pseudoroots need H semisimple as well as G simply connected: SL_3 ⊃ GL_2 at p = 3 has none. Its PGL_2 example shows only that no L-homomorphism is nontrivial on Ĥ.
- Plan the published examples, §§9.4–9.7, as final targets too: cyclic base change, mod 2 Eisenstein series, the exotic transfer from Sp_2n, and SL_3 → G_2.
routes.reason: Sections 8 to 12 are almost pure structure theory of reductive groups in characteristic p: fixed subgroups of an automorphism of prime order, Borel-de Siebenthal and its dual, centralisers of the split part of a gamma-fixed torus, admissible Borels and the parabolic they generate, norm and dual norm maps between tori and their duals, pinned automorphisms with their invariants e_alpha, f_alpha and theta_alpha, exceptional isogenies, and explicit Weyl group and root computations in E_7 and E_8. The Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap is the roadmap in that direction: it plans Borel and parabolic subgroups, root data with their Galois action, pinned Chevalley-Demazure group schemes over Z with their base change and Frobenius on points, and the special isogenies in characteristics 2 and 3. Because it is a Tau Ceti roadmap it is existing work and is never re-planned, so what extends it is a Part II (PROTOCOL section 15). Nothing in it, nor in ReductiveGroupsPartII, plans Borel-de Siebenthal, the endoscopic subgroups of the dual group, admissible Borel classes, dual norms, the C-group and c-group, or the existence of sigma-dual homomorphisms, and no other roadmap goes in that direction. The Theorem of section 8.1 is placed here with the rest of section 8 because its content is the dual norm attached to an admissible Borel class; it imports the Brauer homomorphism itself from the Part II of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces proposed above.

Section 7 is, in the authors' own description, folklore on the Satake transform written out because they know no reference with characteristic p coefficients, and it lands inside layers this roadmap already plans. SR.4 plans the Satake transform for unramified G at a hyperspecial K, the isomorphism with the appropriate invariant algebra on the dual torus retaining the relative Weyl group and Frobenius action, with the coefficients and the q-half normalization to be specified and the unnormalized integral form recorded separately, and the identification of Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters. That is exactly what sections 7.1 to 7.4 and 7.6 supply over k: the twisted action w * a = wa sqrt(Sigma^*_G / w Sigma^*_G)(q_v) of the restricted Weyl group, which removes the need to choose a square root of q_v; the invariant theory lemma identifying W_0-invariant functions on the dual torus with G-hat-invariant functions on G-hat semidirect Frob_v; local pseudoroots as the canonical substitute for the q-half normalization; the Satake parameter of an unnormalized parabolic induction; and Theorem 7.9, which states the isomorphism canonically in terms of the c-group. The correspondence between unramified k^*-valued characters of a torus and elements of T-hat(k) is the base case of the same identification. SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over rings and says explicitly that characteristic p is to be treated in the smooth action category with integral double-coset operators, which is where Fun_G(S x S) belongs; SR.0 plans the smooth category and admissibility over arbitrary coefficients; and SR.2 plans unnormalized induction from a parabolic. This roadmap is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so it may take the paper as a source.

sourceIssues.correction: Run the comparison with a bounded complex. Replace the singular chains C_*(X/K) by a bounded complex of permutation k[σ]-modules that carries the H(G,K)^σ-action and is σ-equivariantly quasi-isomorphic to C_*(X/K). For example, take cellular chains of a finite-dimensional σ-stable, K-equivariant triangulation compatible with all finite levels, as §1.4 suggests ('a compatible triangulation of X'). Alternatively, argue with sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, which uses the hypothesis that X/K has finite cohomological dimension. Either way both spectral sequences then converge to the same homology, and the conclusions of Theorems 4.4, 5.8 and 6.5 follow as stated.
sourceIssues.reason: C_*(X/K) is the singular chain complex (the vertical differential 'is the standard singular differential'), which is unbounded. Each total degree of C^Smith then has infinitely many terms. With the direct-sum totalisation the row filtration is bounded below and exhaustive, so steps (1) and (2) are fine. The column filtration is not bounded below, however, and vanishing of H_j(X/K) for large j does not make vhE converge to the same homology. Example: G = K = 1, and X a locally finite mapping telescope of S^1 ⊂ S^3 ⊂ S^5 ⊂ ⋯ with the free action of σ = ζ_p. X is locally compact, contractible and has a free σ-action. Every singular simplex has trivial stabiliser, so each C_j(X) is k[σ]-free and hvE^1 = 0, giving H_*(Tot) = 0. But vhE^1 = H_0(X) = k in row 0, so vhE^2_{i0} = T^i(k) = k for every i, and with one row there are no further differentials. Thus vhE^∞ ≠ 0 does not compute H_*(Tot), although H_*(X) vanishes in positive degrees. Such an X has infinite covering dimension, so the theorem's hypothesis of finite cohomological dimension excludes it. The proof, however, never uses that hypothesis beyond the vanishing of H_*(X/K) in high degrees. The same step recurs in the proof of Theorem 6.5, with cochains. sourceIssues.correction: Supply the argument that Γ_F → Out(H) is the mod 3 cyclotomic character. σ is F-rational, so Γ_F fixes σ ∈ Z(H)/Z(G) ≅ Z/3 and acts on its dual Q(G)/Q(H) by ±1 according to its outer action. Evaluation at σ is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism Q(G)/Q(H) → μ_3, so γ acts nontrivially on H exactly when γ(ζ_3) = ζ_3^{-1}.
sourceIssues.reason: The verification of (9.7.2) on p. 226 uses 'γ projects to o ⟹ cyclo(γ) = −1', and it would fail for γ acting trivially with cyclo(γ) = −1: ρ^-_H(γ) and ρ^-_G(γ) would differ by β_{1,*}(−1) inside the torus L̂_1 = T̂.
